entries.name: AWS architecture artwork
entries.summary: Render and browse the bundled AWS architecture artwork with names, theme variants and provenance.

document.purpose: Render and browse the bundled AWS architecture artwork with names, theme variants and provenance.
document.behaviorProvider: Manifest-backed local images and a native catalogue composed with shared controls.

component: Look up artwork by the manifest-backed typed name. Invalid runtime names render nothing; getAwsLogoUrl returns an empty string for an unknown name.
Keep original artwork in image elements. Use the manifest light asset and an optional official dark variant selected by the CSS theme mapping; preserve source colors and geometry.
Use the manifest name as image alternative text unless label overrides it. decorative produces an empty alternative when surrounding text already names the symbol.
host: Supply permitted manifest ids and meaningful nonduplicated labels; do not imply that artwork usage grants trademark permission or product endorsement.
Own authorization, usage-policy review and updates to the vendored asset release. Preserve ATTRIBUTION and checksums when replacing the artwork.

requirements.statement: Look up artwork by the manifest-backed typed name. Invalid runtime names render nothing; getAwsLogoUrl returns an empty string for an unknown name.
Keep original artwork in image elements. Use the manifest light asset and an optional official dark variant selected by the CSS theme mapping; preserve source colors and geometry.
Use the manifest name as image alternative text unless label overrides it. decorative produces an empty alternative when surrounding text already names the symbol.
AwsLogoCatalog owns local query, kind, category, page and selected-logo state. Search matches all query words across name, id and category; filter changes reset pagination.
Clamp catalogue page size between twelve and one hundred twenty, with a finite default of sixty. The selected logo can remain visible while filtered results change.
Copy the selected manifest id through the clipboard and expose success/failure status. Download links point to the local bundled SVG asset; no remote asset refresh occurs.
Supply permitted manifest ids and meaningful nonduplicated labels; do not imply that artwork usage grants trademark permission or product endorsement.
Own authorization, usage-policy review and updates to the vendored asset release. Preserve ATTRIBUTION and checksums when replacing the artwork.
Keep the frame and catalogue in iconography group tokens; genuine nested inputs/buttons keep their owning category. Do not recolor third-party artwork to match a project brand.

limitations: This vendored artwork family has an authored contract but no standalone generated API family; the public TypeScript declarations remain authoritative.
No new artwork, remote update, endorsement, brand customization or rights verification is supplied.
Source coverage does not certify visual, assistive-technology or trademark-policy acceptance.

entries.name: Button
entries.summary: A native button for an action, with independent size, intent, emphasis, and loading state.

document.purpose: Activate an action, with intent independent of emphasis.
invariants: Use a native action element. Navigation belongs to Link.
Loading prevents duplicate activation and preserves the accessible name.
Keyboard focus remains visible in both modes.
document.behaviorProvider: native-button

component: native action semantics and safe default type
disabled/loading rendering
intent/emphasis and icon composition
host: meaningful accessible action name
event handling, async operation state and native form intent
safe authorization and routing choices

requirements.statement: Render a native button with default type=button; forward native button attributes and event handlers while owning disabled/loading semantics and visual data attributes.
Choose type=submit explicitly when submitting a form. Use Link for navigation and keep action authorization/business effects in the caller.

Set native disabled when disabled or loading is true and expose aria-busy while loading. Preserve the label DOM; without a leading icon hide label/trailing-icon paint by opacity and center a spinner, otherwise replace the leading icon with the spinner.
Supply meaningful text or aria-label/aria-labelledby, including for icon-only use. Loading preserves existing label content but cannot create a useful name from unnamed children.
Represent intent, emphasis and size independently with data attributes; default to default intent, primary emphasis and medium size without changing native interaction behavior.

Native disabled/loading prevents activation. aria-disabled alone supplies styling/semantics but the plain native Button does not suppress its handlers; a composing primitive or host must implement that behavior.
Use an instance-specific gradient identifier for nonprimary AI icon foregrounds and a hidden SVG definition; clone supplied React icon elements only to apply the intended stroke style.
Retain trigger-group keyboard focus indication in both modes and forced-color treatment. Use group tokens for state geometry and palette, and verify actual focus/contrast in the rendered context.

limitations: The component does not await onClick, own pending state or prevent duplicate requests before the host sets loading.
Disabled native controls may lose focus; no explicit focus recovery, confirmation or authorization policy is supplied.

host: Supply a meaningful group name and explicit button types. Use ToggleGroup or SegmentedControl when exclusive selection is required.
Keep action order and emphasis consistent across the product; authorization and action completion belong to the host.

Own permission decisions and sensitive-data policy. Clipboard availability depends on browser permissions and context.

entries.summary: An ordered series chart that emphasizes magnitude with a filled area beneath the line.

document.purpose: Present ordered quantitative series as a area chart with shared loading, legend, tooltip and optional exact-data support.
document.behaviorProvider: Recharts Cartesian chart primitives and shared ChartContainer.

component: Delegate loading, error and empty presentation to ChartContainer; empty means no data or no series. Loading precedes error, error precedes empty, and the chart only renders in the remaining branch.
When showLegend is true, render real aria-pressed toggle buttons backed by local hidden-series keys. Toggling changes plotted visibility without removing records from the optional data table.

Enable the Recharts accessibility layer and name the plot with its title and arrow-key inspection instruction. Optionally expose a native disclosure containing exact stringified records in ChartDataTable.
host: Supply ordered records with stable series keys and numeric values matching xKey and each series key. The wrapper does not sort, fetch, aggregate or validate Cartesian values.

Enable showDataTable or provide an equivalent exact-data alternative when users need detailed values. Supply domain-appropriate title, units and formatters; default numeric labels use en-GB formatting.

requirements.statement: Supply ordered records with stable series keys and numeric values matching xKey and each series key. The wrapper does not sort, fetch, aggregate or validate Cartesian values.

entries.summary: A schedule view of tasks, milestones, progress, and dependencies across a day, week, or month scale.

document.purpose: Display an inclusive UTC calendar schedule with scale navigation and optional task selection.
document.behaviorProvider: Native SVG/layout and shared SegmentedControl; local gantt-model validation.

component: Use ganttModel to reject empty/duplicate IDs, invalid calendar dates and end-before-start records, showing their labels in a status notice. Dates are validated as exact YYYY-MM-DD UTC calendar days.

Use controlled scale when supplied, otherwise initialize local scale from defaultScale. The segmented control updates local state only uncontrolled and always calls onScaleChange when provided.
host: Own editing, persistence, selectedTaskId and dependency correctness. Supply today explicitly for a deterministic marker; this chart does not schedule, drag-resize, resolve cycles or update the current date.

Expand week bounds to Monday-based weeks and month bounds to calendar months. Display an explanatory replacement rather than a grid when the padded interval exceeds 366 times five days.
Render bars as named buttons only when onTaskSelect exists; emit the normalized task and derive aria-pressed from selectedTaskId when supplied. Otherwise render noninteractive role=img task bars.
Draw known nonself dependency edges decoratively; include dependencies in task labels and exact schedule data. Unknown dependency IDs remain textual references and do not create paths.

Provide a native schedule-data disclosure with task/start/end/progress/owner/dependency headers. Show a today marker only for a valid explicit date inside the model range.

limitations: No critical-path calculation, dependency-cycle validation, work calendars or task editing.
Large row counts are not virtualized even within the bounded calendar span.

entries.summary: A summary value with an optional unit, percentage comparison, and compact supporting trend.

document.purpose: Summarize one named metric, optional unit, change and small trend while keeping the meaning of favorable movement explicit.
document.behaviorProvider: Native read-only content composed with Card, Skeleton, Sparkline or MiniBarChart.

component: format value and delta
derive trend presentation from explicit favorability
replace data with a named loading state
host: accurate metric units and comparison period
data loading and failures
meaningful trend labels and favorable-direction decision

requirements.statement: Render the supplied label visibly and as the Card aria-label; loading marks the Card aria-busy.
Format numeric values with Intl.NumberFormat using en-GB and the supplied format options; render string values as supplied. Append a truthy unit without calculating or converting the value.
Omit comparison when delta is undefined or nonfinite. A finite delta renders a signed percent with at most one fractional digit and the supplied comparison label.
Arrow direction follows delta sign, but success/destroy treatment follows trendIsPositive when given and otherwise whether delta is positive. Zero is always neutral and described as unchanged.

Set trendIsPositive when a decrease is beneficial or when product semantics differ from positive-is-good. Supply delta as an already-computed percentage; the card does not derive it from value or prior data.
Include screen-reader text describing unchanged, favorable or unfavorable change alongside the signed delta. Decorative direction arrows are aria-hidden.

With sparkline supplied, bar selects MiniBarChart and other variants select Sparkline. Explicit intent controls the chart accent independently of favorability; otherwise neutral uses function and nonneutral uses the derived trend.
While loading, retain the label and render a named status with skeletons instead of value, chart and comparison. Do not leave stale metric content presented as the current value in that branch.
Supply accurate deltaLabel and sparklineLabel when the data is not the default previous/last 24 hours. Model missing or failed metric data explicitly; there is no dedicated error or no-data prop.

MetricCard-owned typography and spacing use data-display tokens even though its API family name includes charts. Card, Skeleton and nested chart components retain surface, feedback and data-viz ownership respectively.

limitations: MetricCard is distinct from ChartMetricCard and does not provide a detailed chart, calculation engine or data-fetch lifecycle.
The value is not normalized for nonfinite numbers; callers must choose truthful missing/error content.
Default comparison and trend labels assume a 24-hour period and must be overridden when inaccurate.

entries.name: Sparkline
entries.summary: A lightweight SVG trend designed for compact summaries without animation or interactive focus.

document.purpose: Render a compact noninteractive visual summary of a nonnegative numeric series with an accessible text label.
document.behaviorProvider: Native SVG geometry and Aegis data normalization, with shared Skeleton for loading.

component: bounded dimensions and normalized samples
compact SVG geometry and image label
loading and empty replacements
host: valid series meaning, scale expectations and accessible summary
finite intended dimensions and nonnegative data domain
separate exact values or detailed chart when required

requirements.statement: Map each nonfinite sample to zero and clamp each finite negative sample to zero before computing geometry or the default label. Do not claim preservation of signed data.
Use group-token default dimensions when absent or nonfinite and clamp finite dimensions to token minimums. Explicit dimensions determine the SVG viewBox and empty/loading footprint.
Loading takes precedence over data and returns a named status containing a Skeleton. An empty nonloading series returns a dash image labeled with label or No activity data.
A populated SVG uses role=img and label when supplied; otherwise describe bucket count, latest normalized value and peak. No title, axis labels or exact-value table is added.
For line/area a single sample is a centered dot; multiple samples form a line and area adds a baseline closure. Bars use zero-based normalized heights relative to a peak of at least one.

Treat line/area geometry as a compact locally normalized trend, not a shared quantitative axis. Supply a detailed chart or exact-data alternative when users must compare magnitudes across independent sparklines.

Supply a label that states the actual quantity, time range and useful trend summary when the generic event-bucket text would be inaccurate. Decorative use and surrounding redundancy require an explicit accessibility decision.

The implementation adds no animation, focus target or pointer interaction. General SVG props are forwarded only in the populated branch, so callers must not rely on those props being retained for loading or empty replacements.
Generate a per-instance id for the AI gradient so multiple sparklines do not intentionally share a gradient definition. Other intents render with their group-token currentColor.
Use data-viz group tokens for palette, dimensions and geometry defaults; keep nested Skeleton styling in its feedback group. Do not bypass group ownership through caller style overrides.

limitations: Negative values are clipped and nonfinite values become zero; this is not a signed or missing-data-preserving chart.
There is no interactive tooltip, keyboard exploration or exact-value table.
Generic SVG props including className/style are not applied to the empty or loading replacement nodes.
Explicit labels can override the generic data summary and therefore must remain truthful.

entries.name: DataGrid
entries.summary: A typed record grid with sorting, selection, column controls, expansion, grouping, pagination, and virtualization.

document.purpose: Browse a supplied local dataset with sortable columns, row selection, optional details, local pagination and optional virtualization.
anatomy: data rows with optional selection and expansion controls
states: column sorted, resized, reordered or pinned
document.behaviorProvider: TanStack Table and Virtual provide row models and measured rendering; Aegis implements row keyboard handling and composes shared Checkbox, DropdownMenu and Pagination controls.

component: local sorting, column state, expansion and pagination
row focus, selection requests and measured virtualization
body-state precedence and toolbar integration
host: stable unique row identities and meaningful labels
fetching, filtering, mutations and complete local dataset
controlled selection/density acknowledgment and custom cell interaction semantics

requirements.statement: Supply stable unique getRowId values and meaningful rowLabel values; selection, expansion, keyed rendering and focus restoration use those identities. Keep custom cell controls independently named.

selectedRowIds controls the selection when supplied; otherwise defaultSelectedRowIds initializes internal selection. Selection changes emit all selected ids and only matching row objects from the currently supplied data.

A controlled host must feed accepted selectedRowIds back and decide whether ids absent from current data remain selected. Bulk-action row objects cover only records present in data, not unavailable server records.

The supplied data is locally sorted and paginated by default. Pagination derives its total from data.length and clamps a rendered page after data shrinks; pagination=false presents the supplied rows without local page slicing. pageSize initializes internal page state rather than controlling later page-size changes.

Loading replaces body rows with skeletons and marks the grid busy; otherwise a truthy error replaces rows with the error EmptyState and optional retry action; otherwise zero displayed rows renders the empty state. Loading disables pagination but is not a blanket lock on every toolbar or header control.

When a key originates on the row itself, Up/Down/Home/End move row focus, Enter invokes onRowClick, Space toggles enabled selection, and Right/Left expand or collapse eligible details. Events from nested controls do not execute those row shortcuts.
A row click invokes onRowClick only outside recognized interactive descendants and when no text selection exists. The host must supply actual navigation or detail-opening behavior.

When supplying renderToolbar, render its selectionActions in the intended selection mode and connect density and visibility through the supplied toolbar API. Custom bulk actions must implement their real operations and call clear when appropriate.

Column menus provide pinning, sorting, hiding and movement alternatives to drag; movement stays within a pinned or unpinned group, and the built-in visibility controls preserve at least one visible data column. Resize handles support Arrow keys, Shift larger steps, Home/End bounds and Enter autosize.

Virtualization is requested explicitly or defaults on above 200 supplied records, and is inactive during loading/error or with no entries. Row focus scrolls the target into view; detail rows have separate measured entries. Resize observers, drag listeners and resize listeners are cleaned up on unmount.

Provide the complete local result set and apply filters before passing data. Fetching, error recovery, remote pagination, authorization and persistence of user column preferences are host responsibilities; the grid does not implement those services.

Use data-display group tokens for grid-owned visuals and density; nested Checkbox, DropdownMenu, EmptyState and Pagination retain their own groups. Preserve dimensions across the four theme/mode mappings and verify the actual scroll container.

limitations: This baseline covers DataGrid, not the record-specific DataGridPresentation demonstration or every data-grid cell family.
Sorting, expansion, column state and pagination are initialized internally; they are not a general externally controlled or server-side grid protocol.
Row-oriented keyboard handling is not an editable spreadsheet or full two-dimensional cell navigation model.
No browser run, visual acceptance or comprehensive accessibility certification is implied by these source-backed requirements.

entries.summary: A semantic set of labels and values for inspecting record or configuration details.

document.purpose: Present record metadata as semantic term/value pairs with a deliberate missing-value treatment.
document.behaviorProvider: Native dl, dt and dd semantics with CSS grid layout; no interaction state.

strict missing-value substitution
responsive column presentation
host: stable unique item identities

requirements.statement: Render a dl with one wrapper containing dt and dd for every supplied item, preserving array order.
Supply a stable unique id per item so React can retain item identity when metadata changes. The component does not detect duplicate ids.
Use emptyValue only for null, undefined or the empty string. Preserve numeric zero; do not convert all falsy values into missing content.
Format booleans or other domain values into meaningful React content before passing them. false is not classified as missing and React renders it without visible text.
An empty items array renders an empty dl rather than an EmptyState or a loading message. emptyValue applies to individual descriptions, not the whole collection.
columns chooses one, two or three top-level tracks and orientation selects stacked or horizontal term/value pairs; these settings do not alter the supplied semantic order.
At the narrow breakpoint, the list collapses its top-level columns to one. Horizontal orientation still uses its paired inner grid, and values allow long content to wrap.

Provide understandable labels and appropriately formatted values; supply named shared controls when a value is interactive. DescriptionList does not infer editable fields, copy behavior or navigation from text.
Own loading, failures and recovery outside the list; keep missing individual values distinct from unavailable entire records. The component has no async state machine.
Use data-display group tokens for term/value typography, spacing and tracks. Preserve native description-list semantics and theme-invariant dimensions when extending the layout.

limitations: No loading/error view, editing behavior or value formatting is provided.
The API exposes className rather than arbitrary root DOM props; outer labeling or region semantics belong to the host.
A missing-value fallback is not applied to false, whitespace-only strings or empty React fragments.

component: URL and raster MIME policy
text-safe metadata presentation
image failure fallback and lightbox composition
host: trusted file metadata and authorization
download response headers and blob lifetime

requirements.statement: Render inline previews only for PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF and BMP MIME types with an allowed URL. Use native img; do not execute or embed HTML, SVG, PDF or office documents.
Reject control characters, executable/file protocols and non-raster data URLs. Permit relative, HTTP(S), blob URLs and base64 raster data URLs; suppress both image and download for rejected URLs.
Render file name and MIME/date metadata as text in a definition list. Format nonnegative safe-integer byte counts in binary units and reject invalid numeric sizes.
After the thumbnail reports an image-load error, show the fallback status and omit the image-preview action for that URL while retaining an allowed download link.
Open supported images through the shared Modal with the file name as title and Image preview description, delegating modal focus management, Escape and close behavior.
When enabled and URL is permitted, render a native download link with the supplied file name and the shared external-link isolation behavior. Download=false removes that action.

Supply authorized URLs and correct MIME/size metadata. Revoke object URLs when no longer used and serve documents with appropriate Content-Type, Content-Disposition and origin policy; URL classification is not content inspection.
Provide imageAlt that describes meaningful image content when the file name alone is insufficient, and supply any already-formatted modification date explicitly.
Use data-display group tokens for the file surface. Nested Button, Link and Modal retain their own category token ownership.

limitations: PDFs and all non-raster documents use metadata/download fallback; no document parsing or browser PDF embedding is provided.
Cross-origin download behavior is controlled by browser and response headers; the download attribute is not a guarantee.
The URL policy is not malware scanning, content verification, DRM or an authorization boundary.

document.purpose: Present relative time with a machine-readable instant and an absolute timestamp tooltip.
document.behaviorProvider: Intl relative/absolute formatters and shared Tooltip; local clock interval.

entries.name: SortableList
entries.summary: Reorder a controlled vertical list using pointer dragging, keyboard dragging or explicit move actions.

document.purpose: Reorder a controlled vertical list using pointer dragging, keyboard dragging or explicit move actions.
document.behaviorProvider: dnd-kit core/sortable sensors and collision strategy, plus shared IconButton controls.

component: identity validation and reorder calculation
real pointer/keyboard drag sensors
move action boundaries and announcements
host: stable unique IDs and accepted order
persistence and concurrent updates
custom item content accessibility

requirements.statement: Reject empty or duplicate string IDs. Use IDs as React keys and sortable identities independently of display labels.
Render items in the supplied order and emit an ordered ID array with activeId, overId and drag or move-button source. Do not mutate the input array or keep a second accepted order.

Use PointerSensor and KeyboardSensor with sortableKeyboardCoordinates, a vertical list strategy and closest-center collision detection. Bind sensor listeners and attributes to the actual named drag-handle button.
Provide drag instructions and live announcements for pick-up, target position and finish/cancel. Space starts and drops keyboard dragging; Escape cancels through dnd-kit.
Provide named up/down IconButtons that emit adjacent moves. Disable up for the first item, down for the last item, and all reordering controls when disabled.
Do not emit a reorder for a cancelled drag, missing drop target, same active/over ID or disabled list.
Snapshot IDs/order on drag start. If the supplied order changed by drag end, decline the move and announce that no move was applied.
Accept emitted ID order by reordering the same stable records and persist separately. Keep IDs stable across renames; reject unauthorized changes and resolve concurrent server updates in the host.
Give the list a useful name and each item a descriptive label even with renderItem. Custom interactive content must remain usable outside the dedicated drag handle.
Use data-display group tokens for list/item layout and preserve nested IconButton trigger ownership. Drag transforms are measured runtime coordinates, not fixed design values.

limitations: One vertical list only; no cross-list transfer, nested tree, virtualization or multi-select dragging.
There is no optimistic persisted state or server synchronization. Explicit move announcements describe a requested move, which the host may reject.
Rows intentionally have no animated reorder transition; the host should verify unusually tall or complex custom items.

requirements.statement: no-results defaults to filter recovery copy, no-data to first-record/source copy, and error to failed-loading/retry copy. The default preset is no-results; compact changes presentation rather than condition semantics.

Use feedback group tokens for the empty-state icon, typography and layout while shared action components retain their owning groups. Keep semantic feedback distinct from decorative surfaces.

entries.summary: An independent boolean or mixed selection control with an optional label and description.

document.purpose: Choose an independent boolean value or display an aggregate mixed state with a form-compatible checkbox.
anatomy: native form input managed by Base UI
document.behaviorProvider: Base UI Checkbox rendered as a native button, with a React tri-state adapter and shared useFieldControl metadata.

component: Checked/mixed rendering and boolean activation requests
Native-form integration and local reset listener
Name/description association and disabled/readOnly delegation
host: Meaning of the boolean or aggregate selection
Controlled state updates and group aggregation
Accessible labeling and validation/submission effects

requirements.statement: Resolve checked from the controlled prop or internal defaultChecked, default false. Map true to primitive checked and indeterminate to the primitive indeterminate prop; the mixed display is not treated as checked=true.

Forward the primitive boolean next value through onCheckedChange and update internal state only when checked is undefined. Mixed state must be supplied or derived by the host rather than inferred from children.

When uncontrolled, attach a reset listener to the native input owner form and restore defaultChecked. Remove that listener when the dependency set changes or the component unmounts; controlled state is not reset by this listener.
Pass name, value, form and resolved required to the Base UI root/input integration; forward the public ref to the rendered button, not to the internal input.

Delegate disabled and readOnly to Base UI and expose aria-readonly for read-only controls. A read-only checkbox remains focusable while refusing pointer/keyboard changes; disabled is a separate unavailable state.

Preserve the Base UI checkbox keyboard model on the native button, including Space activation. The linked story exercises Space, read-only immutability and disabled state; it does not establish that Enter toggles.
Resolve shared Field attributes, associate the optional visible label, and merge optional description ids with caller and Field descriptions.
Update controlled checked when accepting a change. For select-all or aggregate use, compute true, false or indeterminate from the actual collection and implement changes to that collection.

Provide a meaningful label or explicit accessible name, a name for form serialization when needed, and any application validation message. required/invalid flags do not authorize or perform a product action.
Use the input group for checkbox-owned geometry and styling, distinguish mixed from checked, and preserve keyboard-visible focus without adding a pointer-only focus ring.

limitations: Checkbox is not a tri-state cycle: ordinary activation emits a boolean; the host owns mixed-state derivation.
Enter is left to Base UI/native-form semantics and is not specified here as a toggle key.
Linked read-only and select-all story assertions are scoped checks, not current execution evidence or full native-form certification.

requirements.statement: Generate a control ID unless id is supplied; render the wrapper at controlId-field and label at controlId-label with htmlFor targeting the control ID. Provide the same metadata through the nearest Field context.

Compose a control that consumes useFieldControl or applies the equivalent ID/ARIA attributes. Field does not clone arbitrary children or automatically associate a plain input that ignores its context.

useFieldControl resolves id, aria-labelledby, required and disabled from explicit control props before context. aria-invalid takes precedence over explicit invalid, then contextual invalid; explicit false overrides inherited booleans.
Merge and deduplicate whitespace-separated contextual help/error IDs with caller aria-describedby IDs, retaining context references before caller references.

Render help for any value except undefined/null/false, including zero and empty string. Render error except undefined/null/false/empty string, including zero; present an existing error with role=alert.

Default contextual invalid and wrapper data-invalid from error presence, while an explicit invalid boolean overrides that inference. Error text is associated through describedby even if invalid is explicitly false.
Show required marker and hidden required wording when required; otherwise show Optional when optional. Required wins if both flags are supplied.

Own validation timing, native required application, server errors, disabled behavior of any nonparticipating children and submit/focus workflow. A context flag is metadata until the control applies it.

Supply a useful label and appropriate control identity; avoid multiple controls accidentally sharing the same generated control ID. A nonempty programmatic name is a host obligation, not runtime-validated by Field.
Use input group tokens for the Field wrapper and retain the nested control behavior/styles rather than replacing them with decorative markup.

limitations: Field is not a form validator or native disabled fieldset. Arbitrary children do not inherit browser control behavior from its div wrapper.
Help/error nodes can contain arbitrary React content; the host must keep messages and any supplied ID references meaningful.

entries.name: InlineEdit
entries.summary: Edit a single committed text value through an explicit local draft, validation, save and cancel lifecycle.

document.purpose: Edit a single committed text value through an explicit local draft, validation, save and cancel lifecycle.
document.behaviorProvider: React local draft and operation guards; shared TextInput, Field and Button behaviors.

component: local draft and focus lifecycle
validation and save operation guard
safe generic failure feedback
host: committed value and persistence
concurrent server updates and authorization
accessible naming and product validation

requirements.statement: Enter editing with a snapshot of the current value, focus and select the native TextInput, and keep subsequent typing in a local draft.
Enter outside IME composition and the Save action validate then save; blur does not commit. Escape or Cancel discards the draft except while a save is pending.
Reject required whitespace-only drafts and truthy synchronous validation messages before onSave. A thrown validator becomes the configured generic error rather than exposing exception text.
Exit an unchanged valid draft without calling onSave. Cancel and successful completion restore focus to the edit button when that button remains mounted and focusable.
Permit at most one in-flight save. Pending disables the input and Cancel, makes the root busy, and displays saving status; the shared Save button is loading.
Retain the failed draft and present the configured error when onSave rejects. Ignore completion state updates from an operation invalidated by unmount.
If the controlled value differs from the entry snapshot before save, block the callback and show conflictMessage; Cancel returns to the latest host value.
Disabled blocks entering or saving and disables an open input. Read-only omits Edit in display state and prevents editing/saving an already-open draft; neither prop silently commits it.

Update value after accepted persistence and use previousValue for server-side concurrency protection. The local pre-save comparison is not a transaction and cannot detect a remote change occurring during the request.
Own form submission and errors beyond this one field. InlineEdit provides no named native submission field and its actions do not submit an enclosing form.
Use input group tokens for the wrapper; nested Field, TextInput and Button retain their own category styling.

limitations: Synchronous validation only; onSave may be asynchronous. No debounce, autosave or blur-save policy.
A pending operation cannot be cancelled through this control; aborting network work and server concurrency belong to the host.
Required validation uses a default English message; product localization and richer field validation need the host callback.

entries.name: NumberInput
entries.summary: Nullable numeric entry with locale-aware display, native form participation and optional shared step buttons.

document.purpose: Enter a nullable numeric quantity with locale-aware formatting, optional step actions and native form participation.
document.behaviorProvider: Installed @base-ui/react NumberField Root, Group, Input, Decrement and Increment; shared Aegis useFieldControl and IconButton.

component: Primitive composition, numeric state and interaction delegation
Visible input ref and raw-number form participation
Field association and optional shared step actions
host: Controlled state acceptance and domain validation
Meaningful accessible naming and locale choices
Submission, persistence, finite configuration and financial precision decisions

requirements.statement: Delegate numeric state to Base UI NumberField. A supplied value selects controlled behavior and preserves null as empty; otherwise defaultValue initializes uncontrolled state. Null defaultValue maps to the primitive empty default rather than zero.

Pass onValueChange and onValueCommitted directly to Base UI without dropping their value or event details. Change details preserve primitive cancellation and reason information; commit callbacks report interaction completion, not persistence.

Pass name, form, min, max, step, required, disabled and readOnly to NumberField.Root. Its associated numeric input owns the submitted raw number. The visible input uses the primitive text-editing behavior and has no duplicate form name. The forwarded ref targets the visible input; hiddenInputRef targets the associated numeric input.

Delegate min/max, step, smallStep, largeStep, snapOnStep, allowOutOfRange and allowWheelScrub to NumberField. Keep its arrow-key stepping and defined Home/End bounds; showSteppers only controls the two rendered increment/decrement actions.
Pass locale and Intl format options through to NumberField so localized display and numeric value remain distinct. The wrapper adds no currency conversion, decimal accounting or precision arithmetic.

Use useFieldControl to resolve the real input id, required, disabled, invalid and description references. Associate a standalone visible label when provided; explicit aria-labelledby takes precedence. Enclosing Field help/error references are merged with an explicit aria-describedby.

Render NumberField.Decrement and NumberField.Increment through actual IconButton components when showSteppers is true. Supply localizable action labels and preserve the primitive button interactions and Tab-sequence policy.

When value is provided, update it to accept requested changes, including null. Supply finite meaningful bounds, valid positive step amounts and valid Intl options. Treat defaultValue as initialization, not a reset command.

Own domain validation, error messages, financial calculations, submission and persistence. invalid and Field.error present host decisions; a committed callback does not certify validity. When allowing out-of-range input, decide how native validity and recovery messages are surfaced.

Supply a standalone label, enclosing Field label or input accessible name. Localize step action names where needed. Do not use placeholder text as the label or override the text-input role to claim unsupported spinbutton semantics.

Keep the owned root and input styles within the input token group; real nested IconButton components retain trigger tokens. Preserve keyboard-visible focus, forced-colors indication and stable size metrics across both themes and modes.

limitations: This is a source-backed requirement record, not a current browser result or release approval.
The wrapper adds no native form-reset listener, application validation, asynchronous validation or persistence.

Intl precision options may round committed values. The component does not provide arbitrary precision accounting or currency conversion; compact notation is unsuitable when edited values must round-trip.

Primitive numeric parsing and keyboard behavior remain dependent on the installed Base UI version. The visible element is a text input with a number-field role description, not an added spinbutton role.

requirements.statement: Start each mounted instance with native input type password. Reveal and conceal change that same TextInput's type between text and password without replacing the value model.
Forward value, defaultValue, onValueChange and native onChange unchanged to TextInput. Visibility changes update only local visibility state and must not synthesize value-change events.
When value is supplied, accept edits through a change callback and feed the resulting value back. defaultValue initializes the uncontrolled value; it is not a later reset command.

Forward the public ref to TextInput's native input and preserve ordinary input properties and lifecycle handlers, including name, form, autocomplete, required and validation constraints. Reserve type and suffix for password visibility and keep clear controls disabled.

Use the same effective Field control id and disabled precedence for the input and visibility action. Let TextInput retain standalone or Field labeling, merged descriptions, required and invalid metadata; explicit control props retain useFieldControl precedence.

Render a real IconButton with type button, an action name that changes between Show password and Hide password (or supplied labels), and aria-controls referencing the native input. Its decorative icon is hidden from assistive technology.

Activating the native visibility button with pointer, Enter or Space changes visibility without submitting the surrounding form or deliberately moving focus away from the button. Normal input and form behavior remains with TextInput and the host.

Effective disabled state disables both input and visibility action. readOnly is forwarded only to the input, deliberately allowing visibility changes without edits. Disabling an already revealed field does not automatically conceal it.

Keep visibility as local instance state through ordinary rerenders. No controlled visibility prop, blur concealment or form-reset visibility handler is provided; a newly mounted instance starts concealed.

Supply a meaningful input label and autocomplete intent appropriate to current or new passwords. Own validation, submission, recovery, authentication and storage; concealment is not encryption or access control.

Preserve input-group styling for TextInput and wrapper-owned icon dimensions; the genuine nested IconButton retains trigger-group styling. Do not override child internals or introduce theme-specific dimensions.

Check keyboard naming, reveal without submission, ref focus, disabled Field integration, read-only reveal and unchanged values across theme changes. Verify dimensions and focus treatment across all four theme/mode mappings rather than treating static markup tests as full acceptance.

limitations: No password strength analysis, authentication, secure storage or asynchronous submission is implemented.
Read-only values remain revealable. Disabled state blocks interaction but does not conceal a previously revealed value.
Visibility is local and not controlled externally; no automatic conceal-on-blur, navigation or form-reset behavior is promised.
Static rendering and linked story code are separate from executed browser, visual or accessibility evidence.

entries.summary: Edit schema-based rich text with bold, italic, lists, links and undo/redo using a mature text editing engine.

document.purpose: Edit schema-based rich text with bold, italic, lists, links and undo/redo using a mature text editing engine.
document.behaviorProvider: Tiptap 3.32.1 / ProseMirror with limited StarterKit schema; Base UI Toolbar and shared Modal/TextInput/Button.

component: schema validation and JSON state bridge
formatting and link commands
Field associations and disabled policy
host: accepted document state and persistence
content validation and form lifecycle
safe downstream rendering and document migration

requirements.statement: Validate initial and controlled JSON with the installed editor schema. Require a doc root; reject unsupported nodes, invalid nesting and unsafe link destinations. Accepted output is normalized editor JSON.

Delegate editing, selection, composition, clipboard schema parsing and history to Tiptap/ProseMirror. Provide bold, italic, bullet-list, numbered-list, link, undo and redo commands through shared buttons.

Initialize uncontrolled content from defaultValue once. Emit document JSON on editor updates. For controlled value, reconcile mismatched editor content without emitting an update or adding the replacement to history.
Use Base UI Toolbar keyboard navigation and expose active formatting through aria-pressed. Mouse toolbar activation preserves the editor selection and commands focus the editor.

Disable automatic linkification and click navigation in the editing surface. Accept HTTP(S), mailto and relative links; reject control characters and other protocols. The dialog preserves its draft on invalid input; empty input removes the selected link.

Use Field control identity, disabled, required, invalid and description associations. Render the editing surface as a multiline textbox; a visible standalone label supplies aria-labelledby when no explicit label association is supplied.
Disabled and readOnly make the editor noneditable and disable formatting actions. Disabled removes the surface from sequential keyboard focus and excludes the named hidden input from form submission.

When name is present, submit one hidden JSON string, optionally associated with the supplied form. Required is announced on the editor; a hidden input does not implement native nonempty-content validation.

Feed accepted document changes back to value. External replacements can reposition selection; coordinate revisions and persistence outside the editor rather than treating this as a collaborative document protocol.
Validate meaningful document content before submission and validate/sanitize downstream rendering according to the application. The link policy and restricted schema are not a general HTML sanitizer.
Use input group tokens for editor presentation and preserve nested toolbar Button and Modal token ownership.

limitations: No tables, headings, media, file upload, comments, collaborative editing or raw HTML value API.
Editor initializes on the client; server-rendered output does not contain an interactive ProseMirror editor.
Toolbar and link-dialog copy is currently English. The host must supply a meaningful editor name.

entries.name: SearchInput
entries.summary: A searchable text field that separates immediate draft changes from debounced search requests.

document.purpose: Capture a search query immediately and optionally emit a debounced search callback.
document.behaviorProvider: Composition of TextInput with a React-managed debounce timer; native input behavior remains with TextInput.

component: Immediate query entry and native search semantics
Cancellation of superseded pending timers
Clear action and display-only shortcut hint
host: Result computation, fetching and asynchronous race handling
Accessible query name and result announcements
Controlled updates, shortcut registration and submission policy

requirements.statement: Compose TextInput with type search, a decorative Search icon and a forwarded input ref. The type, prefix and suffix are owned by SearchInput rather than exposed as replacement props.

Use controlled value or local text initialized from defaultValue. onValueChange is called immediately for edits, and the inherited native onChange remains immediate; debounce applies only to onSearch.
For a query different from the last emitted query, schedule onSearch after Math.max(0, debounceMs), defaulting debounceMs to 250 milliseconds.
Cancel the pending timer when query or debounceMs changes and on unmount. Read the current onSearch callback through a ref when the timer fires.
Initialize lastEmitted from the initial query so mounting alone does not emit onSearch. A later controlled value change follows the same debounce path as a user edit.
Preserve TextInput labeling, Field metadata, native form attributes, disabled/readOnly behavior and clearing. clearable defaults true and the clear label defaults to Clear search.
When passing value, accept edits by updating it through the immediate change callback. Keep the input draft distinct from any delayed search results.

Implement result filtering or requests, loading/error/empty states and result announcements. Cancel or ignore stale asynchronous results in the host; clearing a pending timer cannot cancel an onSearch request that already began.
Give the search input an accessible name and implement any advertised keyboard shortcut in the owning page. shortcut renders a kbd hint only; SearchInput does not register a shortcut handler.
Keep SearchInput-owned styling in the input group and preserve the nested TextInput behavior and keyboard focus treatment across modes.

limitations: Debounce cancellation applies to pending timers, not network requests, promises or search side effects already started.
No initial search, Enter-to-search override, result list, loading indicator or search service is supplied by this component.
TextInput native-form reset limitations also apply to the locally stored SearchInput query. Existing linked checks are bounded story assertions, not certification.

entries.name: SegmentedControl
entries.summary: A compact, mutually exclusive choice implemented with native radio inputs.

document.purpose: Select one value from a short related option set using a labeled native radio group.
document.behaviorProvider: Native HTML fieldset, legend and radio inputs with React state and input-focus modality tracking.

component: Native radio grouping and label association
Initial default selection and value-change notifications
Group/option disabled states and presentation flags
host: Meaningful group and option labels
Stable option identities and controlled state
Application effects and any stable form serialization

requirements.statement: Render a fieldset with a visually hidden legend from label. Render each option as a labeled radio and use one generated useId name for the native radio group.
Initialize local state from defaultValue when supplied, otherwise from the first non-disabled option, otherwise the empty string. Display value instead when a controlled value is supplied.
On a radio change, update local state only when value is undefined and notify onValueChange with that option value. Set each radio checked state by equality with the selected string.
Disable the fieldset for a disabled group and individual radio inputs for option.disabled. Expose disabled/selected attributes on option wrappers for their corresponding styles.
Keep native radio keyboard behavior and focus tracking. The keyboard story selects Monthly and uses ArrowRight to check Quarterly.
Expose size, fullWidth and wrap as presentation attributes while retaining the same fieldset/radio interaction model.

Supply unique stable option values and meaningful option labels. Keep a controlled value in the current available option set and reconcile removed/disabled options in the host; the component does not automatically repair a stale selection.

Update value when accepting onValueChange. If stable native-form naming is needed, serialize the selected value explicitly in the host: this API does not expose name, form or required, and its internal generated radio name is not a product field contract.
Use the radio-group selection for a related choice and implement any associated view or data change in the host. Do not assume tabs, tabpanels, routing, readOnly or validation semantics are supplied.
Use input-group tokens for owned styles, retain native radio keyboard focus, and preserve size metrics when theme or mode changes.

limitations: The public API has no readOnly, name, form, required or invalid prop. Disabled is not a substitute for a focusable read-only contract.
The initial local selection is not recomputed just because options or defaultValue change later; the host must reconcile dynamic option sets.
The keyboard story is a bounded native-radio assertion, not a full tab-widget or native-form acceptance suite.

entries.name: Select
entries.summary: A single-value picker with grouped options, optional icons, descriptions, and native form integration.

document.purpose: Choose one stable string value from a supplied option set using a form-compatible popup listbox.
document.behaviorProvider: Base UI Select and DirectionProvider, with local controlled/uncontrolled adapters and shared useFieldControl metadata.

component: Single selection and independent popup-open state adapters
Base UI form/keyboard/dismissal delegation
Option grouping, descriptions, selected display and empty option state
host: Valid stable option identities and accessible names
Controlled value/open updates and application validation
Application effects of a selected value

requirements.statement: Display the supplied value or local defaultValue, defaulting to the empty string. Pass an empty selected string to Base UI as null and translate a null value callback back to the empty string.
Resolve open independently from value using open or internal state initialized by defaultOpen. Update internal state only when open is undefined and forward onOpenChange as a boolean notification.
Pass name, form, autoComplete, readOnly and resolved required/disabled into Base UI Select.Root for its form-compatible input behavior.

Use Base UI Trigger/List/Item/Popup to delegate typeahead, Arrow/Home/End navigation, option activation, Escape dismissal and focus return. The keyboard story specifically exercises ArrowDown/Enter selection and trigger focus return.
Delegate disabled controls, disabled options and readOnly selection locking to Base UI. readOnly is not a promise that the popup cannot open or be browsed; it prevents value changes.
Apply the standalone label or Field/explicit label references to the trigger; associate optional descriptions to their options using ids derived from the resolved control id and encoded option value.
Render distinct option group labels in first-occurrence group order. With no options, render a disabled No options available item rather than a selectable fallback.
Use the explicit dir when supplied or the inherited Base UI direction, and render the popup through a portal with token-backed offset and collision padding.

Provide unique nonempty option value strings, meaningful labels, and values that correspond to the available option set. Empty string is reserved for no selection; the wrapper does not validate or repair duplicate, empty or unknown option identities.

When controlling value or open, update the corresponding prop from its callback. Own validation/error messages and the application action caused by a selection; the wrapper does not save or fetch records.
Provide a visible label, enclosing Field or explicit aria-label/aria-labelledby for the trigger. Do not use placeholder or the generic option-list fallback name as the control name.
Use the input group for Select-owned styles and fixed geometry, preserve Base UI focus guards and portal behavior, and keep control metrics consistent across all four theme/mode mappings.

limitations: This is a single-string selection contract, not free-text entry, multi-selection or an action-menu contract.
Base UI behavior is delegated; this record and its linked checks do not certify every browser, form reset or assistive-technology combination.
onOpenChange and onValueChange expose values only; the wrapper does not expose the primitive event-details cancellation API through those callbacks.

entries.name: Switch
entries.summary: A binary on/off control for a setting, with a label that remains stable across states.

document.purpose: Present a named on/off setting with Base UI switch semantics and optional native form participation.
anatomy: native form input managed by Base UI
document.behaviorProvider: Base UI Switch rendered as a native button with shared useFieldControl metadata.

component: Boolean checked state delegation and callback forwarding
Switch semantics, thumb state and native-form attributes
Label/help association and disabled/readOnly delegation
host: Meaning, timing and persistence of the setting
Controlled updates and application error handling
Accessible name and form submission policy

requirements.statement: Pass checked, defaultChecked and onCheckedChange directly to Base UI Switch.Root. Expose boolean on/off state; no indeterminate state is part of the public Switch API.
Render the primitive root as a native button and forward the public ref and supported remaining button props to that button.
Retain Base UI/native-button activation for the switch. The ImmediateSetting story exercises a click followed by Space; the story description also documents Enter activation.
Pass resolved disabled and readOnly to Base UI so unavailable controls and focusable non-editable controls remain distinct states. Do not implement a separate local toggle that bypasses those props.
Forward name, value, form and resolved required to the primitive input integration. The documented form behavior includes the checked state when a name is provided.

Associate the optional visible label with the resolved control id; merge the optional description with caller and Field descriptions. Forward explicit label/invalid references through useFieldControl.

When supplying checked, update it from onCheckedChange when accepting the requested change. Own persistence, rejected updates and user feedback; switching the visual control does not perform a network save.
Provide a persistent name describing the setting through label, Field or an accessible name on the button. Do not depend on the thumb position alone to communicate meaning.
Own validation messages and native-form submission behavior. required and invalid are metadata; the switch does not determine whether the setting is permitted or save its value.
Keep switch-owned styling and fixed defaults in the input group, preserve keyboard focus visibility, and keep dimensions stable across the four theme/mode mappings.

limitations: This contract does not turn an immediate-setting presentation into automatic persistence or authorization.
Controlled/uncontrolled form behavior is delegated to Base UI; there is no additional Aegis reset handler or mixed-state model here.
Linked story assertions cover a small interaction fixture and are not certification of every form, keyboard or assistive-technology case.

entries.summary: A multiline native text control with optional measured growth and a character count.

document.purpose: Enter multiline text with optional bounded automatic growth and a character count.
document.behaviorProvider: Native HTML textarea with React state, measured growth and shared useFieldControl metadata.

component: Native multiline editing and forwarded textarea ref
Value callbacks and optional measured growth
Associated label, descriptions and character count
host: Accessible naming and validation decisions
Controlled value and submission/reset behavior
Appropriate rows, maxRows and content limits

requirements.statement: Display value when supplied or local text initialized from defaultValue otherwise. Changes update local state only when value is undefined, then call onValueChange and onChange.
Render a native textarea with rows, maxLength and supported remaining textarea attributes, including name, form and readOnly; forward the public ref to that element.
Resolve required, disabled, invalid and ARIA references through useFieldControl. Associate the optional visible label and merge the counter id into aria-describedby when showCount is enabled.
When showCount is enabled, render text.length with the optional maxLength denominator. This count uses JavaScript UTF-16 code units, not grapheme clusters or bytes.

When autoGrow is enabled, calculate height from computed line height, padding, border and scrollHeight, bounded by rows and maxRows; switch vertical overflow to auto when content exceeds the upper bound.
Recalculate growth when text or relevant sizing props change and when ResizeObserver detects a width change; disconnect that observer on effect cleanup.
Retain native multiline keyboard editing and pass disabled/readOnly through to the textarea. The wrapper does not bind Enter to submission or provide an Escape action.

Update value in response to accepted edits when using controlled mode. Own explicit reset behavior and validation of supplied programmatic values; native maxLength is not a programmatic-value truncation service.
Provide a label, Field or explicit accessible name, including when appearance is plain inside another composition. Supply meaningful error descriptions and sensible positive rows/maxRows.
Use the input group for owned styles and fixed design defaults, retain keyboard-visible focus, and preserve size and font metrics across the four theme/mode mappings.

limitations: The existing AutoGrowAndCounter story links a typing/count assertion; it does not certify all growth, resize, Unicode or native-form cases.
The wrapper has no explicit native form-reset synchronization listener.
Character counting is not grapheme-aware. Neither a counter nor an invalid flag validates application content.

Controlled or local value display and change callbacks
Field metadata association and conditional clear action
host: Accessible naming and meaningful validation messages
Controlled state updates and application submission
Meaning and behavior of supplied adornments

requirements.statement: Display value when it is supplied; otherwise initialize local text from defaultValue. An input change updates local text only when value is undefined, then calls onValueChange with the string and onChange with the native-input React change event.
Render a native input, default type to text, forward the input ref, and pass supported input attributes such as name, form, autoComplete and constraints through to that input.

Use useFieldControl to resolve id, required, disabled, invalid and description references. A standalone label is associated through htmlFor and aria-labelledby; explicit aria-labelledby takes precedence.
Forward readOnly to the native input and resolved disabled to the control. Show the clear button only when clearable is true, text is nonempty, and the control is neither disabled nor read-only.

The clear button is type button. Clearing uses the native value setter and a bubbling input event, returns focus to the input, and calls onClear; the existing change handlers remain the value-change path.
Leave text editing, selection, Tab focus and native form keyboard behavior on the input; this wrapper adds no Enter or Escape command handler.
When supplying value, update it from onValueChange or onChange to accept edits, including clear requests. Treat defaultValue as the initial local value rather than a reset command.
Provide a meaningful standalone label, enclosing Field label, or accessible name on the input. Placeholder text and decorative prefix/suffix content do not replace that name.
Own validation decisions, error text and submission effects. invalid and aria-invalid expose state; they do not compute an application validation result.
Keep owned styles in the input group, retain keyboard-visible focus, and preserve size and font metrics across Fundamental/Fundamental Floating and light/dark modes.

limitations: This baseline is a source-grounded requirement record, not a current browser result or approval.
The wrapper stores even its uncontrolled value in React state and does not install an explicit native form-reset listener. Do not infer a synchronized reset guarantee from defaultValue.
Clear behavior is described for supported text-like native input types; this contract does not certify every possible HTML input type or custom event override.

entries.name: TimeRangePicker
entries.summary: A period selector that commits a relative preset or a validated absolute UTC interval.

document.purpose: Choose a relative time preset or explicitly apply an absolute UTC range.
document.behaviorProvider: Aegis Popover/Button, react-day-picker and time-range helpers.

component: Use a TimeRange union: relative preset or absolute from/to strings. Relative presets are 15m,1h,24h,7d,30d; resolution uses the supplied now or current time. Default is relative 24h.

Choosing a preset commits immediately and closes. Opening resets the custom draft from the current value; custom calendar/time changes remain draft until Apply. Dismissal therefore does not commit a custom draft.
Render the custom calendar in UTC, derive date/time fields from UTC ISO slices, and emit absolute ISO strings ending in Z. The trigger formats absolute ranges with UTC explicitly.
Disable Apply unless both endpoints parse and start is not later than end. Current helper permits equal endpoints even though the visible recovery copy asks for end after start.
Associate trigger with Field name, descriptions and invalid state; when disabled, prevent opening/committing and force the rendered popup closed. Resolve open/close state locally.
host: Own the controlled range, persistence and refresh cadence. Supply valid ranges and a stable now for reproducible relative previews; interpret relative presets as rolling durations rather than calendar-day boundaries.

entries.name: TreeView
entries.summary: A hierarchical multi-selection tree whose branch check states are derived from selectable leaves.

document.purpose: Choose selectable leaf IDs from a hierarchical tree with independent expansion and derived tri-state branches.
document.behaviorProvider: Aegis tree model helpers and custom native ARIA tree composition.

component: Store selected leaf IDs in controlled/default state. Branch state is derived from descendants; mixed branches toggle to fully selected. Disabled ancestors/leaves do not participate in selection propagation and existing disabled selections remain unchanged.

Keep expanded IDs independent from selection; deduplicate expansion updates. Only expanded descendants enter visible navigation order. Controlled/default values are initialization/ownership boundaries, not persistence.

Provide roving focus with Up/Down, Home/End, Right expansion/child navigation, Left collapse/parent navigation, Enter/Space selection, Ctrl/Meta+A selection and * sibling expansion. Printable-key prefix search uses a 500ms buffer.

Render tree/treeitem/group roles, aria-multiselectable, checked/mixed states, expansion, level, position and set size. Decorative checkbox marks are aria-hidden; expand buttons are outside the Tab order.
When a controlled collapse removes the focused node, choose a visible enabled ancestor. Restore DOM focus only when focus fell to document.body, avoiding theft from another focused control.
host: Supply a finite acyclic tree with unique stable IDs, meaningful labels and selected leaf IDs. Own search/filter data, lazy loading, virtualization, authorization and persistence; no native form name or submission adapter is provided.

entries.name: ResizablePanels
entries.summary: Composable split panes backed by react-resizable-panels, with labeled resize handles.

document.purpose: Expose the resizable-panels behavior library through group, panel and labelled separator components.
document.behaviorProvider: react-resizable-panels Group, Panel and Separator; Aegis adds styling and collapsed descendant semantics.

component: primitive prop forwarding
collapsed inertness
labelled handle and focus styling
host: panel layout constraints
accessible names
persistence and surrounding workspace

requirements.statement: Forward GroupProps through ResizablePanels and PanelProps through ResizablePanel; sizing, pointer gestures and separator keyboard mechanics belong to react-resizable-panels.
Mark a panel inert and aria-hidden when its reported percentage is zero; initialize this state from a zero defaultSize and preserve explicitly supplied inert/aria-hidden values.
Update collapsed state before forwarding each panel onResize callback with size, id and previous values.
Require a label for ResizeHandle and apply it as the separator accessible name; the optional default grip is decorative.
Track pointer-versus-keyboard handle focus for presentation while forwarding supplied capture handlers. This does not replace the primitive keyboard implementation.
Supply compatible direction, panel identifiers, default/min/max sizes and collapsible constraints through the primitive API; give the group a usable bounded layout.
Name each handle for the adjacent content and account for focus when collapsing a panel containing the active control; inert hides descendants but does not implement a product-specific fallback.
Persist and restore layout through host state or the underlying library API when required. The Aegis wrapper does not choose a storage key or save sizes itself.
Own pattern or component styling consumes layout group tokens. Nested shared components retain their own group ownership; do not restyle their internals.

limitations: Behavior follows the installed react-resizable-panels version; this contract does not certify every upstream interaction.
No automatic persistence or arbitrary descendant focus handoff on collapse.
All group/panel sizing constraints remain the host responsibility.

entries.summary: A menu attached to a content region, opened through a context gesture or keyboard command.

document.purpose: Expose contextual actions, nested menus and controlled checkable choices from a single trigger.
document.behaviorProvider: Base UI ContextMenu and optional DirectionProvider with Aegis keyboard opening and Tab-exit handling.

component: menu entry composition
keyboard opening
controlled/default visibility and focus exit
host: action execution
controlled checked/radio values
trigger and action discoverability

requirements.statement: Support controlled open/onOpenChange or local defaultOpen and forward disabled to Base UI. The trigger receives tabIndex=0 and aria-disabled when disabled.
Handle the ContextMenu key and Shift+F10 on an enabled trigger, anchor opening near its bounds and focus the popup. Pointer/touch context behavior delegates to Base UI.
Compose actions, groups, separators, submenus, checkbox items and radio groups from DropdownMenuEntry data; delegate menu navigation and disabled-item behavior to Base UI.
Expose indeterminate checkboxes as aria-checked=mixed and request true on their next toggle. Checkbox activation keeps the menu open, while radio activation closes it.
On Tab, request immediate closure and allow normal tab movement from the trigger; suppress normal final-focus restoration for this exit so the next target can retain focus.
Use the trigger as the normal final-focus target and optional DirectionProvider for text direction. The deprecated modal prop is ignored in favor of the primitive native modal behavior.

Supply stable ids, meaningful labels and callbacks; update checked/radio values, handle asynchronous failures and provide confirmation for consequential actions. Shortcut labels do not register shortcuts.
Provide a suitable single trigger accepting refs and primitive props, and expose important actions through a discoverable alternative when users may not know a context menu exists.
Own pattern or component styling consumes trigger group tokens. Nested shared components retain their own group ownership; do not restyle their internals.

limitations: No asynchronous action pending/error lifecycle, authorization or automatic confirmation.
The deprecated modal prop does not change behavior.
The host must apply controlled open changes for Tab exit and other dismissal requests to take effect.

entries.name: DropdownMenu
entries.summary: A compact menu of actions, checkbox choices, radio choices, groups, and nested menus.

document.purpose: Expose contextual actions and optional menu checkbox/radio preferences, grouped items and nested submenus.
anatomy: optional submenu triggers and nested popups
document.behaviorProvider: Base UI Menu primitives with typed recursive menu entries and optional DirectionProvider.

component: Menu entry composition and primitive navigation/dismissal delegation
Checkbox/radio selection requests and per-item close policy
Trigger composition, disabled items and popup naming
host: Action effects and application validation
Controlled open/checkbox/radio updates
Meaningful labels, stable identities and any actual shortcuts

requirements.statement: Forward open, defaultOpen and onOpenChange to the Menu root. Default defaultOpen and modal to false; modal is independently configurable.

Compose the supplied element through Primitive.Trigger. Treat native button elements and custom components as native-button triggers; non-button intrinsic elements use the primitive non-native trigger path.
Render the discriminated entry types as primitive action items, checkbox items, radio groups, submenus, groups or separators. Groups and submenus recursively render their supplied items.

Keep keyboard navigation, typeahead, submenu navigation, Escape dismissal and focus return delegated to Base UI Menu; this wrapper does not replace the menu with a form select or a custom key handler.

Forward an action item onSelect as the primitive Item onClick handler and leave normal action-item closing to the primitive default. intent destroy selects visual treatment; it does not add a confirmation or permission check.

Render checkbox menu items without closing on click. Map indeterminate to aria-checked mixed and a minus indicator, and convert its next activation callback to true; otherwise forward the primitive boolean next value.
Render each radio-group from its supplied value and onValueChange, with individual disabled options and closeOnClick enabled on radio items.
Pass disabled flags to action items, checkbox items, radio options and submenu triggers. A group label or separator is structural rather than an action.

Name the top-level popup from label, default Actions, and render item labels, optional icons and shortcut hints. Apply DirectionProvider only when an explicit dir is supplied; otherwise inherit surrounding direction.

Update open when controlled and update checkbox checked/radio value when accepting callbacks. Supply unique stable entry ids and radio option values; the menu does not store application preferences for controlled entries.

Provide a named operable trigger and meaningful menu/item labels, implement every advertised action and any shortcut key handling, and own destructive-action confirmation or errors. shortcut text is a kbd display only, not a registered command.
Use the trigger group for DropdownMenu-owned styling and icon defaults, including portaled menus and submenus. Preserve Base UI focus/navigation behavior and nested shared component ownership.

limitations: This is an action/menu-preference surface, not a form-compatible single-value Select. It has no public name/form/required/readOnly field API.
Displayed shortcuts and destructive intent are presentation, not shortcut registration, authorization or confirmation behavior.
The current family stories demonstrate states and local callbacks but contain no play assertions; no passing interaction evidence is claimed by this baseline.
Controlled checkbox/radio item state remains with the host, and indeterminate is not a user-cycled third state.

entries.summary: A searchable modal command list with grouped actions and optional global shortcut registration.

document.purpose: Search and invoke host command items in a shared dialog-backed command palette.
document.behaviorProvider: Base UI Dialog and Autocomplete primitives plus local query filtering and shortcut handling.

component: dialog/list composition
query matching
open shortcut and selection
host: commands and side effects

requirements.statement: Support controlled open/onOpenChange or defaultOpen local state. The internal setOpen(false) path clears query; an external controlled close alone need not reset it.

Provide stable command identifiers, meaningful labels and callbacks. Handle promise errors, navigation completion, authorization and destructive confirmation in the action implementation.
Avoid competing global shortcuts and duplicate palettes, apply controlled open callbacks, and provide a discoverable trigger when a keyboard shortcut is insufficient.
Own pattern or component styling consumes navigation group tokens. Nested shared components retain their own group ownership; do not restyle their internals.

limitations: No command authorization, persistence, asynchronous action lifecycle or automatically wired per-item shortcuts.

entries.name: Pagination
entries.summary: Controlled navigation through result pages, with an optional page-size selector.

document.purpose: Present a controlled one-based page position, result range and optional page-size selector for a host-owned result set.
anatomy: numbered page buttons and visual gaps
document.behaviorProvider: Native nav, buttons and select; Aegis calculates a bounded display window from host props.

component: normalize displayed page/range
emit page and size requests
label boundary controls and current page
host: actual paging, fetching and accepted page state
accurate total and page-size options
coordinate loading and asynchronous results

requirements.statement: For display, normalize a finite total to a nonnegative integer, a finite pageSize to at least one and a finite page to the one-based valid range. Nonfinite values fall back to total=0, size=25 and page=1 respectively.
Update page in response to onPageChange and apply it to the underlying dataset or request. Display normalization does not call back to correct invalid host state or fetch records.
The polite summary reports 0 plus noun for an empty total, otherwise the current inclusive item range and total. The page count remains at least one even for zero results.

Disable Previous at the first page and Next at the last page; zero results or disabled disables all page navigation buttons. Each numbered button identifies its page and the current one exposes aria-current=page.

Always include valid first/last pages and the current neighborhood, adding near-edge neighbors as needed, deduplicating and sorting. Gaps render as aria-hidden ellipses rather than navigable controls.

Render the size select only when onPageSizeChange exists. A size change calls onPageSizeChange with the numeric selected value, then calls onPageChange(1); the host must accept both updates coherently.

Supply finite positive integer pageSizeOptions suitable for the dataset. The component deduplicates finite positive choices and includes the normalized current size, but does not integer-normalize the supplied option values.
Pagination buttons use type=button and must not submit an enclosing form. The size control has an associated Rows per page label and uses native select keyboard behavior.
Set disabled while page changes must be blocked and own any focus/announcement policy for newly loaded content. Pagination does not move focus to the result region or provide loading/error UI.
Use navigation group tokens for controls and input-modality focus styling. Keep the display range and disabled semantics independent of theme and density decisions.

limitations: Pagination does not store pages or perform a fetch; the host remains authoritative.
The noun and Rows per page label are not a comprehensive localization API.
Accepted host inputs should be finite positive integer sizes even though the display applies defensive normalization.
