entries.name: SideNav
entries.summary: A collapsible application navigation rail with groups, counts, search, workspace content, and a footer.

document.purpose: Present hierarchical application destinations in an expanded sidebar or collapsed navigation rail while delegating route changes to the host.
anatomy: destination buttons and expandable groups or menus
document.behaviorProvider: Native navigation buttons and Aegis expansion state; collapsed hierarchy uses shared Base UI-backed DropdownMenu and Tooltip.

component: collapse presentation and optional internal collapse state
expanded-group state and active visual markers
named buttons and inert collapsed workspace
host: active route state and real onNavigate effect
unique item ids, contextual labels and icons
search behavior, shortcut registration and custom footer/workspace state

requirements.statement: Own activeId and update it in response to onNavigate after performing the intended route or view transition. Navigation items are buttons, not href links; the component does not integrate a router or browser history.

Expanded leaf buttons invoke onNavigate(id); buttons with nonempty children toggle their child region instead. Expanded active destinations expose aria-current=page and expanded groups expose their controlled region id.

collapsed controls the rail when supplied; otherwise defaultCollapsed initializes internal state. The toggle emits onCollapsedChange and updates internal state, while a controlled host must supply the accepted collapsed value.

Active ancestors initialize expanded groups, and expanding from the collapsed rail merges the current active ancestors into those groups. Changing activeId while already expanded does not automatically expand newly active ancestors.

A collapsed parent with children opens a shared DropdownMenu with recursively nested items. Leaf selection requests navigation and active ancestors mark the parent visually; expanded children are not simultaneously rendered in the rail.

Collapsed destination buttons retain explicit accessible labels and tooltips; hidden workspace content is aria-hidden and inert. The same collapse toggle remains mounted with its updated accessible label.
When search is visible, wire onSearch to a real search interface. The displayed Cmd-K hint is visual content only; the host must register and scope any keyboard shortcut.
Replace or hide the default workspace summary when its fixed avatar, Team workspace subtitle or All systems connected status would be inaccurate. Supplying workspace changes only its displayed name.

The footer receives collapsed state when supplied as a function; the host must make its content appropriate for both presentations and handle route focus transitions or mobile drawer behavior separately.

Use navigation tokens for sidebar-owned layout, icons and active styling; nested IconButton, DropdownMenu, Tooltip, CountBadge and Kbd retain their groups. Verify focus and legibility in both collapse states and all theme mappings.

limitations: No router, Cmd-K listener, responsive modal drawer or automatic route-heading focus is implemented.
There is no selected-item expansion synchronization effect after an external activeId change while expanded.
Default workspace status is illustrative copy, not a health check.

entries.name: Stepper
entries.summary: An ordered progress indicator that can allow return navigation to completed steps.

document.purpose: Show ordered workflow progress and optionally revisit the current or completed steps through controlled navigation.
document.behaviorProvider: Native nav/list/buttons with local roving tab-stop and orientation-specific keyboard focus.

component: state presentation
eligible-step focus movement
step change requests
host: current index and validity
validation and persistence
step labels and identifiers

requirements.statement: Use an explicit item state when supplied; otherwise derive complete/current/upcoming from the zero-based currentStep. Mark the indexed current item with aria-current=step.
Without onStepChange, render informational step content rather than interactive controls. With a callback, render native buttons.
Enable only the current index or steps whose effective state is complete, unless the whole component is disabled. Request a change only for a different enabled step.
Maintain one tab stop among eligible steps. Orientation-appropriate arrows wrap focus, while Home and End focus the first or last eligible step without selecting it.
Expose step number, title and effective state in button labels and hidden state text; visual status markers are decorative.
Supply a valid currentStep, stable unique ids and an onStepChange handler that updates state. The component does not validate bounds or persist progress.
Perform validation, data saves and permission checks before applying requested changes; explicit completed states make earlier or later steps eligible.
Choose orientation and meaningful navigation naming for the surrounding page. Horizontal arrow mapping is physical left/right and is not automatically reversed for RTL.
Own pattern or component styling consumes navigation group tokens. Nested shared components retain their own group ownership; do not restyle their internals.

limitations: No step validation, next/back action, asynchronous lifecycle or automatic progress persistence.
Explicit states may disagree with the indexed current marker; hosts must keep them coherent.
No RTL-specific reversal of horizontal keyboard arrows.

entries.name: Tabs
entries.summary: A labeled set of peer views using Base UI tabs and associated content panels.

document.purpose: Select one view within a shared context using Base UI tabs, with either per-tab panels or one persistent shared content slot.
anatomy: overflow wrapper and named tab list
document.behaviorProvider: @base-ui/react Tabs and DirectionProvider supply tab/list/panel interaction; Aegis owns uncontrolled selection initialization and styling.

component: selection callback adaptation
tab/list/panel composition
shared panel slot identity and decorative icon treatment
host: unique stable values and usable tab labels
controlled state acknowledgment
valid selection when items change and panel content semantics

requirements.statement: Without value, initialize internal selection from defaultValue or the first enabled item. Later changes to defaultValue do not reset internal selection.
With value supplied, forward that selection to Base UI and emit string onValueChange requests without updating internal selection. Non-string primitive changes are ignored.

Use unique stable item values and ensure a controlled or initial value identifies an appropriate enabled item. When items are removed or disabled, reconcile selection deliberately; this wrapper has no reconciliation effect.

Set Base UI List activateOnFocus=true for automatic activation and false for manual activation. Preserve the primitive keyboard and disabled-tab behavior instead of adding independent click-only selection.
Forward orientation and root HTML properties to Base UI Root. An explicit ltr/rtl dir selects the DirectionProvider direction; otherwise use the inherited direction.
Supply a meaningful label for the tablist and accessible item labels. The default Views label is generic; icons are aria-hidden and cannot replace the textual name.

Without sharedContent, render a Base UI Panel for each item value. When sharedContent is defined, render one unkeyed Panel associated with the current active value and place the shared content there instead of item.content.

Use sharedContent for a persistent workspace and keep its component type/key stable if local drafts must survive tab changes. Per-tab inactive-panel mounting follows Base UI defaults; the wrapper does not expose keepMounted or persist each view draft.
Render a count when it is not undefined, display 99+ above 99, and retain the full numeric count in an aria-label. Counts are descriptive metadata rather than selection state.
Use navigation group tokens for the line/pill tab treatments and overflow layout. Presentation changes must preserve Base UI focus behavior, semantic relationships and the selected host state.

limitations: This wrapper does not route, fetch data, reconcile removed active values or preserve every inactive panel draft.
Shared-content state preservation depends on stable caller content identity; it is not persistence across unmounts or routes.
Primitive keyboard and panel lifecycle behavior is delegated to the installed Base UI version, not independently reimplemented or certified by this document.

entries.name: BottomSheet
entries.summary: A bottom-only nonmodal panel for an existing bounded flex-column workspace.

document.purpose: Provide a nonmodal resizable bottom panel inside a bounded workspace.
document.behaviorProvider: Native in-flow region and separator with ResizeObserver, pointer capture and keyboard resizing.

component: bounded height
resize interaction
close requests and conditional focus return
host: workspace sizing
controlled open/height state
content state and routing

requirements.statement: Render in normal document flow without a portal, modal backdrop or focus trap; closed panels return null and unmount their content.
Support controlled open and height callbacks or local default values. Close requests update local state only when open is uncontrolled.
Measure the parent and panel margins with ResizeObserver, reserve workspaceMinHeight, and clamp rendered height between the available bounds.

Use primary-pointer drag to change height and a focusable horizontal separator exposing current/min/max pixel values. ArrowUp grows, ArrowDown shrinks, Shift uses the larger step, and Home/End choose bounds.
Close through the named close button or an unhandled Escape from within the panel. Stop active drag on pointer completion/cancellation, lost capture, blur or closing.

Capture the active opener when opening. When closing or unmounting after focus was inside, restore it only if connected and the document body still owns focus; do not override a new host focus target.
Provide a measurable bounded parent workspace and finite meaningful height constraints. Keep controlled height/open values in sync with callbacks.
Preserve drafts outside the unmounted panel when needed, supply an informative title and handle route transitions or initial content focus; opening does not move focus into the panel automatically.
Own pattern or component styling consumes surface group tokens. Nested shared components retain their own group ownership; do not restyle their internals.

limitations: This is an in-flow nonmodal panel, not a viewport drawer or modal dialog.
No automatic initial focus, route integration or persistence of unmounted content.
Host sizing props must be finite and coherent; unlike Sheet helpers this implementation does not normalize every nonfinite input.

document.purpose: Run a focused modal task with predictable dismissal and focus return.

Use Base UI dialog behavior.

component: Base UI modal composition and controlled/uncontrolled bridge
persistent accessible title/description in hidden-header mode
focus-return safeguard for completed actions
host: meaningful title and task content
accepted open state and asynchronous task lifecycle
intentional focus destination when opener disappears

requirements.statement: Use Base UI Dialog Root with modal behavior and portaled Backdrop/Popup; an optional trigger is rendered through the primitive Trigger. Forward open/defaultOpen and lifecycle/trigger handle options to the primitive.
Render Primitive.Title in either visible header or screen-reader-only mode. Associate an optional truthy description through a generated ID and Primitive.Description in both header modes.
Provide a meaningful title even when showHeader=false and review nested task semantics. ReactNode title is required by type but empty content is not runtime rejected.

Delegate initial focus, modal keyboard interaction and normal return focus to Base UI. At close, finalFocus declines restoration when a completed action has already focused an element outside the popup other than document.body; otherwise allow primitive restoration.

Expose a named primitive close button by default and allow it to be hidden. closeOnOutsideClick defaults true; explicit disablePointerDismissal takes precedence over its inverse. These options do not themselves disable Escape.

Render non-null/undefined children inside a named focusable Dialog content region; render truthy footer and headerActions in their own slots. showHeader=false keeps title/description semantics while omitting visible header actions.
Feed accepted onOpenChange values back when controlled and handle async failures, destructive confirmation and state preservation in the host or the separate ConfirmDialog component.
ModalClose delegates to Primitive.Close; deprecated asChild requires a single valid React element, while render supports native primitive composition.
Use surface group tokens for modal geometry/backdrop/focus presentation. Nested controls keep their own categories; review focus return and dismissal in the actual task.

limitations: A focusable surviving opener is not guaranteed; the host must supply a meaningful alternate destination when it is removed or deliberately redirected.
Modal itself does not lock dismissal during async work, submit a form, validate content or own request cancellation.

entries.name: Popover
entries.summary: Anchored interactive content with optional header and footer outside the scrollable body.

document.purpose: Open anchored contextual content with a named popup, optional header/footer, and explicit close composition.
document.behaviorProvider: Base UI Popover root, trigger, portal, positioner, popup and close primitives, with explicit initial/final focus selection.

component: Primitive open/dismissal delegation and anchored placement
Popup/body names and hidden-header semantics
Scoped initial/final focus and close composition
host: Accessible trigger and meaningful popup name
Controlled open state and content validation/submission
Application effects and draft lifetime

requirements.statement: Forward the supported Root props, including open/defaultOpen and onOpenChange, to Base UI. The wrapper does not maintain a separate open-state copy or expose event details in the typed onOpenChange callback.

Render the supplied trigger through Primitive.Trigger and use the primitive popup/close model for activation, Escape and dismissal. The scrollable-body story checks Escape close and return to the trigger.

Name the popup and body from title when supplied, otherwise from label, default Details. When showHeader is false, retain title and description in visually hidden elements and preserve their ARIA references.

On opening, choose the first visible eligible button, link, input, select, textarea or tabindex=0 descendant, excluding the scroll body itself and hidden/inert/aria-hidden ancestors; fall back to the primitive default focus behavior.
Allow primitive final focus unless the current active element is already outside the popup and is not the body; preserve a deliberate external focus handoff rather than always refocusing the trigger.

showClose renders a Primitive.Close with the accessible name Close popover, including a floating close button when the header is hidden. PopoverClose forwards primitive props/ref; deprecated asChild requires one valid React element or throws.
Render children in a separately focusable scrolling region, with optional header and footer outside that scroll container so body scrolling does not move those regions.
Portal the popup and position it with side/align and token-backed offset/collision padding. Apply optional width while CSS constrains the popup to available viewport dimensions.
When controlling open, update it from onOpenChange. Own content state, asynchronous actions, validation, submission and dirty-draft policy; a close request does not save or reset application data.

Supply a usable named trigger that accepts the primitive props/ref and a meaningful title or label. Children containing forms or interactive controls must provide their own form associations, names and disabled/readOnly states.

Use the surface group for popover-owned styles and fixed defaults, preserve nested shared-component styling and primitive focus guards, and retain keyboard-visible focus across the four theme/mode mappings.

limitations: The generic fallback label Details supplies a name but does not establish meaningful product context.
Root open props are forwarded, but Popup initialFocus/finalFocus are owned by this wrapper rather than exposed as public override props.
Popover has no component-level disabled/readOnly or native form field value. Its trigger and nested controls own those semantics.
The linked scrolling/Escape story is a scoped check, not certification of every nested popup, modal configuration or custom trigger.

entries.name: Sheet
entries.summary: A nonmodal, resizable panel that pushes content within its own bounded workspace.

document.purpose: Compose a bounded workspace and a nonmodal resizable side or bottom sheet that pushes its content.
document.behaviorProvider: Native in-flow section and separator with sheet-state sizing helpers, ResizeObserver and pointer capture.

component: workspace and panel layout
bounded sizing
resize and close behavior
host: workspace dimensions
controlled state
content persistence and route focus

requirements.statement: Keep content mounted in the workspace and conditionally mount the sheet at bottom, left or right. No viewport portal, modal backdrop or focus trap is created.
Use controlled open/size when supplied, otherwise local defaults. Emit clamped integer size changes through onSizeChange; nonfinite size falls back to the computed minimum.
Measure the workspace inner axis minus padding and gap, reserve contentMinSize and reconcile minimum/maximum to available space. Lock resizing when both computed bounds are equal.
Capture the primary pointer and resize on the placement axis. Release active drag on completion, cancellation, lost capture, blur, placement change or unmount.
Expose separator orientation and numeric values; grow toward the workspace for the relevant placement arrow, shrink with its opposite, use Shift for a larger step and Home/End for bounds.
Close through its button or unhandled Escape inside the panel. If panel focus would be lost, restore a connected restoreFocusRef or remembered opener only while document focus remains on body.

entries.summary: A right-side detail panel that can be modal or docked beside the workspace.

document.purpose: Inspect contextual content in a modal side overlay or a docked nonmodal aside, with optional record navigation and resizing.
anatomy: optional SideSheetSection and SideSheetField content helpers
document.behaviorProvider: Base UI Dialog for overlay state/trigger and modal behavior; native aside for docked content; measured pointer/keyboard resize logic.

component: Open-state adapter and overlay/docked rendering
Names, close control, scoped focus handoffs and scroll body
Optional bounded resize and record-navigation affordances
host: Record selection, data loading and previous/next updates
Controlled open state, draft lifetime and submission effects
Meaningful title, trigger and content semantics

requirements.statement: Resolve open from the supplied prop or local state initialized from defaultOpen. Update local state only when open is undefined and notify onOpenChange with the requested boolean.

For overlay mode, use a modal Dialog with Portal, Backdrop and Popup. For docked mode, use a nonmodal root and conditionally render an aside in place, without the overlay portal/backdrop; docked mode disables pointer dismissal.

The header close button requests false. Overlay Escape and outside-pointer behavior are delegated to Dialog, with disablePointerDismissal forwarded; docked content closes on an unprevented Escape bubbling inside the aside, not on an outside pointer.

Associate the sheet with its title and optional description ids. Render the body as a focusable region named by the title; use Dialog title/description parts in overlay mode and native heading/paragraph elements when docked.
On overlay opening, request initial focus on the first sheet icon button, normally Close. On closing, allow primitive focus return unless focus has already moved to an element outside the popup.

Docked content does not automatically focus a close control or trap focus. On unmount, restore the remembered connected opener only when focus was still inside the panel and has not already moved elsewhere.

Keep header and optional footer outside the body scroll region. headerActions takes precedence over the backward-compatible actions alias; Section and Field helpers render content structure without application data behavior.

Show navigation when both position and total are supplied. Disable Previous without its callback or at position <= 1, and Next without its callback or at position >= total; announce the position text through a polite live span.

When resizable is enabled, expose a labeled vertical separator with current/min/max values. Pointer dragging and ArrowLeft/ArrowRight change width, Shift uses the larger step, and Home/End select the measured limits; clamp width to configured and available space.

Update controlled open and record-navigation props from callbacks. Own record retrieval, loading/errors, unsaved-change policy, form submission and draft persistence across conditional mounting or closing; the sheet does not save records or veto closure for dirty forms.

Supply a meaningful title and closeLabel, valid one-based navigation position/total, and a usable trigger when needed. Custom trigger elements must preserve the primitive ref and event props; content controls require their own labels and form semantics.

Keep sheet-owned styling and fixed defaults in the surface group, preserve nested shared component ownership, respect reduced motion, and retain keyboard-visible focus and the scoped scroll container.

limitations: Docked mode is not a modal dialog: it has no modal focus trap, overlay backdrop or global outside-pointer dismissal.
onOpenChange exposes only a boolean, not primitive event-details cancellation. Controlled hosts may decline a request by retaining open, but this contract does not supply an unsaved-change workflow.
Resizing is measured local UI state, not persisted preference storage. Existing story assertions cover overlay focus/close/resize cases, not every docked or nested-overlay lifecycle.
No loading, error, empty-record or native form implementation is provided by the sheet itself.

document.purpose: Provide a supplementary description for a single trigger using a positioned tooltip, with an optional richer text layout.
document.behaviorProvider: Base UI Tooltip Provider, Root, Trigger, Portal, Positioner and Popup.

component: description wiring
controlled/default visibility
shared primitive positioning
host: trigger accessibility
supplementary content

requirements.statement: Support controlled open/onOpenChange or local defaultOpen, and use the supplied delay or owning-group delay token through the primitive provider.
Preserve an existing trigger aria-describedby and append the generated tooltip id while visible; render the popup with role=tooltip.
When disabled or content is null/undefined, return the original child unchanged without a tooltip trigger or popup.
Delegate hover/focus opening and dismissal to Base UI Tooltip; forward side and alignment and use group-token collision padding and offset for the portaled positioner.
RichTooltip composes title, description and optional kbd text inside Tooltip; it does not register the displayed shortcut or introduce an interactive popover workflow.
Supply one suitable element that accepts primitive props/ref and is accessible by keyboard when its tooltip is relevant. A disabled native control may require a separate focusable wrapper.
Give the trigger its own accessible name and keep essential instructions available without depending on hover. Use Popover or another suitable pattern for interactive content.
Apply controlled open callbacks and use meaningful supplementary text. The component does not infer whether external content has become stale or whether the trigger is enabled.
Own pattern or component styling consumes feedback group tokens. Nested shared components retain their own group ownership; do not restyle their internals.

limitations: No accessible-name substitute, persistent help surface or shortcut execution.
ReactNode content is flexible; the implementation does not reject interactive descendants, so hosts must choose the correct pattern.
Returning the original child when disabled does not disable that child.

Use flat for an ordinary group that can remain transparent, raised for the default surfaced card and floating when the stronger surface is warranted. Elevation is presentation, not selection or behavior.
Use shared slot padding; when header is immediately followed by content remove the content top padding. Footer layout carries its own top border and action spacing.

limitations: No automatic title association, collapsible state, selection, loading or navigation behavior.
CardTitle is an h3 by default; the host must review heading hierarchy and avoid making a whole card interactive around nested controls.

entries.summary: Filter a dataset without losing the applied query or draft.

document.purpose: Filter a dataset without losing the applied query or draft.
invariants: Immediate mode has no Apply action.
Explicit mode requires Apply and separates draft from applied filters.
Theme changes preserve draft and applied values.
This experiment supports customer query (text) and status (select: all, Active, Trial, Paused); other datasets require a new reviewed pattern contract.

component: finite customer-spec validation and rendering
local draft and applied filters
result count/reset and customer table
host: records and optional explanatory source content
validated composition/profile binding before reuse

requirements.statement: Validate the supplied CompositionSpec and render an alert instead of controls/results when invalid. Supported controls are query text and status select with options drawn from all, Active, Trial and Paused; one or two controls are required.

In immediate mode filter from the current local draft and show no Apply action. In explicit mode keep local draft and applied values separate; Apply copies current pending values into applied state and the result status indicates unapplied changes.
Filter records by locale-lowercased substring across name, domain and owner together, and by exact selected status unless all. Do not trim, sort, fetch or mutate the provided record array.

Use all as the default status if declared, otherwise the first declared option. Reconcile an unavailable stored status to that default; omitted query/status controls stop contributing their respective filter.
Reset and empty-state Clear filters clear query and reset both local draft and applied status to the current default. Empty results retain table structure and add the configured empty message.
Keep draft/applied filters in the mounted renderer while applying declared mode/presentation attributes and table density. Changing those visual props does not intentionally reset React filter state.
Name the section from its heading, announce result count/unapplied state through a status region, and place the native table with scoped column headers in a named focusable scroll region.

Use validateCompositionSpec/resolveComposition for strict known properties, compatible Apply settings and registry/profile revision/hash checks. The renderer validates the spec shape/revision but does not compile a profile or verify a supplied active profile itself.

Provide stable unique record IDs and the declared customer fields/statuses. Records are host-owned; draft/applied filters are local to this mounted renderer and are not exported as a controlled filtering API.

Treat this as the finite customer-directory experiment. Other datasets, controls, remote filtering, loading/error state or persistence need an appropriate reviewed pattern contract, rather than assuming FilterBar behavior applies.
Use filtering group tokens for this composed pattern and preserve nested TextInput, Select, Button and Tag ownership. Keep dimensions independent from light/dark mode.

limitations: This renderer has no controlled draft/applied-state props, pagination, sorting, server filtering or asynchronous data lifecycle.
Unmounting resets local filters. Changing control availability can reveal or hide retained values; route or record-identity reset policy belongs to the host.
Deterministic recipe validation and source-backed requirements do not certify rendered accessibility or arbitrary customer data.

entries.name: AiDiffReview
entries.summary: An explicit approve or reject boundary around an AI-proposed document change.

document.purpose: Review an original/proposed text pair with explicit local approve or reject decisions and asynchronous host callbacks.
document.behaviorProvider: React request lifecycle composed with shared AiCard, DiffView and Button.

component: revision-bound decisions
pending and error presentation
decision focus feedback
host: authoritative side effects
document and provenance accuracy
controlled status reconciliation

requirements.statement: Treat the original/proposed pair as the review revision; changing either aborts the current operation and resets the local review state to pending.
Allow review only while not disabled, not awaiting a decision, status is pending, and original and proposed differ.
Pass original, proposed and an AbortSignal to decision callbacks; approve additionally receives proposed content. Ignore results for aborted or superseded operations.
A failed decision retains a pending review with an error and returns focus to the relevant decision control; success announces the decision and focuses its audit summary.
Support local decisions even when no approve/reject callback is supplied; the status does not prove that an external system changed.
Implement permissions, persistence, audit records and cancellation of remote work. An AbortSignal and ignored UI results cannot undo an already applied side effect.
Supply accurate original/proposed content, provenance, confidence and any controlled status. These displayed facts are not independently verified by the component.
Compose the shared read-only DiffView with collapsed unchanged content and first-change focus support; mode and maximum-height props configure the review presentation.
Own pattern or component styling consumes ai-assistance group tokens. Nested shared components retain their own group ownership; do not restyle their internals.

limitations: Approval is a local UI state, not security authorization or human certification.
No editing, merging, deployment, persistence or independently verified AI provenance.
Hosts must reconcile controlled status and honor cancellation where their backend allows it.

entries.summary: Compose generic controlled collection search, host filter/action slots and a result status without assuming a record model.

document.purpose: Compose generic controlled collection search, host filter/action slots and a result status without assuming a record model.
document.behaviorProvider: Native named section and shared SearchInput; host-rendered filter/action controls retain their behavior.

component: controlled query callbacks
owned search disabled state
result message and responsive slot layout
host: apply criteria and compute resultCount
fetching, race handling and result states
wire slot disabled state and actual actions

requirements.statement: Render the shared SearchInput from query and emit immediate edits through onQueryChange, without keeping a second query state.
Accept query changes, apply filters or requests, compute resultCount and render results. This toolbar has no WorkRecord dependency, fetching, filtering, stale-response handling or result table.
Reject counts that are not nonnegative safe integers. Render singular/plural result text by default, or the complete supplied resultText, in an atomic status region.

busy sets aria-busy on the region and replaces the visible count with busyLabel. It does not disable editing or reset query/filter state; assistive technologies may defer status announcements while the region is busy.
disabled directly disables the owned SearchInput and is passed, with busy, to both optional slot render functions.
Apply the supplied disabled state to filter/action controls, including portaled controls. The pattern does not clone arbitrary children or guarantee a complete lock merely by passing slot state.
Render a section named by label and a search control named by searchLabel, optionally linked to resultsId. Keep normal Tab order; do not expose ARIA toolbar or roving-key semantics.
Keep search, filters, actions and count in that source order. Use a shared token-backed non-growing search basis and natural flex wrapping; do not impose a viewport breakpoint.

Supply meaningful region/search names, a valid result target id when used, localized resultText/busyLabel where needed, and real action behavior. Record the chosen shared pattern for comparable collection pages.
Use filtering group tokens for owned geometry and status styling. Keep nested SearchInput and caller controls in their own groups; do not override internal control styling.

limitations: No automatic dataset wiring, search request debounce or persistence is supplied.
Busy is informational; only disabled locks the owned search, and the host must explicitly disable its slots.
This pattern does not replace DataGrid selection/density/column controls or the WorkRecord-specific FilterBar.

entries.name: FilterBar
entries.summary: A controlled search and table toolbar with mutually exclusive inline or sidebar filter editing.

document.purpose: Edit the shared WorkRecord filter model and expose density and column-view controls, either inline or alongside a host-owned filter panel.
document.behaviorProvider: Aegis recordFilterReducer and controlled host state, composed from shared Base UI-backed controls.

component: translate filter edits to reducer transitions
maintain picker draft and optional internal density
applied summaries and removal focus handoff
host: own accepted RecordFilterState and apply it to records
render and control any external panel
wire density, column visibility and selection actions to the dataset

requirements.statement: All filter edits derive a next RecordFilterState from the current value through recordFilterReducer and emit onValueChange; the bar keeps no authoritative filter-value copy.

Feed accepted changes back through value and apply the same state to the dataset. For WorkRecord semantics, applyRecordFilters uses OR within facets, AND across facets and rules, case-insensitive search and inclusive lastSeen time bounds; FilterBar itself does not fetch or filter rows.

The inline picker prevents native form submission, trims input and rejects blank or disabled commits. Equality choices for supported facets deduplicate facet values; other choices append a rule with an id. Successful commit clears the input and closes the picker.
Changing picker field or operator clears its input. Closing the popover alone does not explicitly reset its field, operator or draft; do not promise discard-on-dismiss behavior.
Panel mode delegates editing and visibility to the host. Supply onTogglePanel, filterPanelOpen and a matching panelId to connect the toggle with the real panel; the bar does not mount that panel.
Show applied criteria when their count is nonzero and either bar mode is active or the external panel is closed. Panel mode with an open panel suppresses this duplicate summary.

Before dispatching a chip removal initiated from its remove button, request focus on the next remove button, then the previous, then the search input. When search is visible and enabled, the final-chip fallback and Clear all can return focus to it. Clear all resets the filter model, including its relative 24-hour time range. Truthy selectionActions hides search while applied summaries may remain, so those search-focus requests do not guarantee recovery after the focused removal control disappears.
Truthy selectionActions hides the normal search/filter row while keeping it mounted. Applied summaries follow their own visibility rules and are not automatically removed by selection mode.

density is controlled when supplied; otherwise an internal default density is updated. Every density activation emits onDensityChange when present. The host must use that density to affect its actual rows.

columns describes host-owned visibility; onColumnVisibilityChange must update the dataset and fed-back column settings. The bar disables choices marked non-hideable or lacking a change callback; it does not itself ensure a data column remains visible.

disabled is forwarded to search, time range, picker trigger/fields, panel toggle, density buttons, column-settings trigger and removable summaries. Column checkboxes in an already-open popover use their own hideable/callback conditions; disabled does not uniformly lock those mounted choices.
Use filtering group tokens for the bar and picker layout while preserving nested control token ownership and shared keyboard, popover dismissal and focus behavior.

limitations: This record-specific filter editor is distinct from the experimental FilteredDataset composition contract.
Search and time-range changes emit immediately; the picker Apply button commits one criterion, not a global deferred filter transaction.
No remote query service, saved-filter persistence or automatic dataset wiring is provided.
The disabled prop does not disable every child in an already-open column settings popover; hosts needing a complete interaction lock must account for that limitation.

In selection mode, the search input is hidden but applied-filter controls may remain visible. Clear all or the last-chip removal can remove the focused control without a visible focus fallback; hosts must review and provide focus recovery for that composition.

entries.summary: A linked, focusable form error summary. It accepts validation results rather than deciding form validity.

document.purpose: Present host-supplied validation errors as a named, focusable summary with links to invalid fields.
document.behaviorProvider: Native React composition with existing shared Aegis controls; see explicit component and host responsibilities.

component: summary structure
explicit summary focus requests
native field link and focus behavior
host: validation and stable error IDs
actual focusable field IDs
revealing hidden fields and custom control focus

requirements.statement: Supply errors from application validation. The summary does not infer validity, mark controls invalid or decide when to validate.
Reject duplicate or empty error IDs and empty field IDs. Render no summary when the supplied list is empty.
Render each message through the shared Link with an encoded fragment targeting the supplied field ID. React escapes message text.

For ordinary unmodified activation, focus the element found by its exact ID and scroll it into view; alternatively call the supplied focusField callback. Modified activations retain native link behavior.
Provide a visible focusable field target. For hidden tabs, composite controls or asynchronously revealed fields, use focusField to reveal and focus the correct control.
A changed, defined focusRequestKey focuses the summary when errors exist. Ordinary rerenders with the same key do not steal focus.
Change focusRequestKey after failed submission when appropriate. The component intentionally does not force an alert role or automatically focus on each validation edit.
Keep owned summary structure in feedback tokens; nested Link retains trigger tokens and focus styling.

limitations: No validation engine, field mutation, router handling or automatic error dismissal.
A field that is missing, disabled, hidden or not focusable needs host handling.
Programmatic focus is an explicit caller request, not evidence that all assistive technologies announce identical text.

entries.summary: Group related labeled form controls in a native fieldset with an associated description and responsive field layout.

document.purpose: Group related labeled form controls in a native fieldset with an associated description and responsive field layout.
document.behaviorProvider: Native fieldset/legend and ContentGrid; nested field controls and the surrounding host form retain their behavior.

component: native group semantics and description ids
responsive grid delegation
native disabled boundary and explicit slot order
host: field values, names, labels and validation
surrounding form, submission/reset and persistence
portaled/custom-control disabled state and action semantics

requirements.statement: Render a native fieldset with the supplied legend as its first child. Render no nested form and add no synthetic form submission handler.
Give a present description a unique id and merge it with the caller aria-describedby through the shared deduplication helper.

Render direct children through ContentGrid, default maxColumns to one and minItemWidth to regular. Use its existing accepted column caps and minimum-width options and let it collapse with container width.
Forward disabled to the native fieldset and keep the field grid and optional action region inside it. Do not clone children or write disabled props into their component state.

Keep legend content noninteractive. Native fieldset rules exempt first-legend descendants and do not automatically cover portaled/custom widgets; pass explicit disabled props to those controls as needed.
Provide individual Field labels or other accessible names and native field names/constraints. A group legend and description do not replace each control label or validation message.
Own the action slot behavior. Set type=submit only for intentional submission of the surrounding form, and type=button for ordinary actions; the section does not supply Save/Cancel or reset policy.
Keep controlled drafts, validation, reset, loading/error/success state and data persistence in the form owner. Closing or disabling this group does not save, reset or validate fields.
Keep legend, description, field grid and actions in document order, with no added surface, sticky footer or child-control style overrides.
Use page-structure group tokens for owned type and spacing, preserve nested control token ownership, and keep geometry consistent across all four theme/mode mappings.

limitations: The disabled boundary is the native fieldset boundary, not an assurance that arbitrary portaled controls are disabled.
ContentGrid caps columns rather than forcing them; deeply nested fields remain the host composition responsibility.
No form element, validation engine, field-state store, persistence or automatic reset is provided.

entries.name: PageHeader
entries.summary: A consistent page title hierarchy with optional back navigation, breadcrumbs, metadata, actions, and secondary content.

document.purpose: Provide a page heading, navigation context, metadata and explicit actions in a responsive structural header.
document.behaviorProvider: Native header and heading elements, with shared Link, Button and Breadcrumb for navigation.

component: heading element and id
back-versus-breadcrumb precedence
responsive arrangement of host content
host: heading hierarchy and meaningful page context
real navigation and action effects
async feedback and route focus handoff

requirements.statement: Render h1 by default or the requested h2/h3 and assign headingId when supplied, otherwise a generated id. The header does not automatically name an outer page landmark.
Choose headingLevel and a stable headingId appropriate to the surrounding document. Route transitions must implement any desired focus or announcement handoff; PageHeader does not focus its heading.
When back is present, render it instead of breadcrumbs, even when both are supplied. Without back, only a nonempty breadcrumb collection creates the navigation row.
A back destination with href renders the shared Link; a callback destination renders the shared Button and invokes that callback. The component does not infer browser-history navigation.
Supply working links for navigation and buttons for actions. Model loading, disabled and failure states in those supplied action controls; the header has no pending-operation state.

Optional leading content precedes the heading; description and metadata follow it; actions follow the summary in document order; children render below the main row. Optional wrappers render only for truthy slot values. A numeric zero can render as text without its wrapper, so the host must format such content intentionally.
Provide metadata with enough textual context to explain status or count and give supplied icon-only actions accessible names. Arbitrary ReactNode slots do not acquire domain meaning from the header.
The main row wraps, title and description can break long text, and the narrow breakpoint gives summary and actions full width without reordering their DOM.
Keep tabs, filters and action controls in the provided slots on their shared implementations; preserve their own state and interaction semantics across layout/theme changes.
Use page-structure tokens for header spacing, typography and icons; nested Button, Link and Breadcrumb retain their own groups. Theme changes must preserve heading dimensions and action order.

limitations: PageHeader is structural; it does not manage routing, browser history, authentication or asynchronous actions.
headingId is an identifier, not a focus API, and arbitrary content is not semantically validated.

entries.name: PageLayout
entries.summary: Initial library choices for collection, detail, settings, and dashboard pages. PageHeader owns the heading and actions. PageLayout adds transparent region wrappers without page padding or child styling. ReadingColumn provides 55ch/65ch/75ch starting measures. ContentGrid uses a container-responsive maximum of one to four columns. Products can propose additional recipes through review.

document.purpose: Compose named page regions using four initial task-specific recipes, explicit reading measures and adaptive grids.

PageLayout.header: PageHeader owns title, description, actions, metadata, leading, back, breadcrumbs and heading props.
PageLayout.slots: header is generated from header props; children is main; filters, aside and footer are optional only where supported.
PageLayout.collection: Optional filters/footer; available width; no aside, reading measure or grid options.
PageLayout.detail: Optional labelled aside/footer; main then aside; no filters or page-level reading measure/grid options. Use ReadingColumn explicitly within main for prose.
PageLayout.settings: Optional footer and measure; one reading column; no filters, aside or grid options.
PageLayout.dashboard: Optional footer, maxColumns and minItemWidth; no filters, aside or page-level measure; direct children become grid items.

ReadingColumn.scope: Explicit prose/form region, not an entire collection or data grid.

ContentGrid.scope: Adaptive grid; maximum is a cap, not a forced count.

validatePageLayoutRecipe.input: JSON object with archetype and optional slots/measure/maxColumns/minItemWidth/asideLabel. Unknown keys fail.
validatePageLayoutRecipe.returns: Array of structured issues; empty means this selection is supported.
validatePageLayoutRecipe.slotValidation: When slots are supplied, header/main are required; duplicates and unsupported slots fail; a detail aside requires a nonempty label. Omitting slots does not assert actual rendered content exists.
validatePageLayoutRecipe.excluded: Does not validate React nodes, DOM semantics, visual quality, data state, route completeness, keyboard workflows or accessibility of nested content.

invariants: Use the same shared PageHeader implementation through every PageLayout recipe.
Named regions follow header, optional filters, main, optional aside and optional footer order.
Collection results use available width and preserve their own scrolling and toolbar behavior.
Only the initial detail recipe allows an aside; main and aside form at most two regions and stack in that order in narrow containers. This is not a universal two-column limit.
Settings use an explicit readable measure; dashboard grid caps are one through four and adapt to the available container.
The shell owns page padding. PageLayout adds no surface, routing, persistence, fetching, selection or form state.
Each nested shared component retains its own style tokens and interactive behavior.
The consuming application owns the document main landmark, data states and actual task semantics.
limits: These four recipes are an initial library, not an exhaustive classification of pages. Unsupported tasks may require another reviewed recipe.
Reading measures are starting points, not universal readability guarantees.
Configuration validation cannot replace browser interaction, geometry, accessibility and visual review.

requirements.statement: Import PageLayout, ReadingColumn, ContentGrid, pageLayoutRecipes and validatePageLayoutRecipe from the declared public importPath. Read recipeSource/portableRecipes and the page-composition guidance for the same supported recipe decisions.

Require archetype, title and children by the public props union. Render a named section with the shared PageHeader and heading ID, then optional filters, main content, optional labelled aside and optional footer in that order.

Collect supplied non-null/non-undefined/non-false optional slots and validate their recipe configuration at render time; throw TypeError for unsupported configuration. Header/main are always declared structurally, so null children are not detected as missing task content.
Collection permits filters/footer and available-width main content; reject aside, measure and grid options. Keep collection overflow and toolbar behavior inside its supplied data component.

Detail permits a labelled aside/footer, with main before aside and at most those two recipe regions. Reject filters and page-level reading/grid options; use ReadingColumn explicitly within main for prose.

Settings wraps children in ReadingColumn with optional measure and footer; reject filters, aside and grid options. ReadingColumn accepts compact/comfortable/wide and defaults comfortable; unsupported measures throw.

Dashboard wraps direct non-null children into ContentGrid items and permits maxColumns/minItemWidth/footer; reject filters, aside and page-level measure. ContentGrid accepts caps one through four, defaults four, and accepts small/regular/large minimums with regular default.

validatePageLayoutRecipe returns structured issues for unknown keys/unsupported options, duplicate or forbidden slots, missing header/main when slots are supplied, and an unlabelled detail aside. Omitting slots does not assert actual rendered content exists.

Use page-structure group tokens; detail regions stack main before aside in narrow containers and grid maximum columns is a cap rather than a forced count. Reading measures are explicit starting points, not universal readability guarantees.

Own the document main landmark and outer page padding. PageLayout adds structure without a surface, routing, persistence, fetching, selection or form state; nested components retain behavior and category tokens.

Review real React content, DOM semantics, data states, route completeness, keyboard workflows, geometry and visual quality. A valid recipe selection alone cannot establish those properties or human approval.

limitations: These four recipes are an initial library, not an exhaustive classification of pages. Unsupported tasks may require another reviewed recipe.

Configuration validation cannot replace browser interaction, geometry, accessibility and visual review.

Change version for every authoritative record change and enforce expectedVersion atomically at persistence. A matching client version alone cannot prevent server races.

Pass recordId, expectedVersion and AbortSignal to onSave; accept its authoritative record/version result, or retain the draft and show rejection text. Reject a result when a different newer incoming version arrived during the save.
Use one native edit form, call reportValidity before saving, and wrap fields in a native disabled fieldset during pending or disabled state. Supply the same disabled state to renderFields.

Return independent drafts, a reliable equality comparator and individually named field controls. Explicitly disable portaled/custom controls using renderFields.disabled and provide domain validation before accepting a save.

Capture the version when deletion is requested. Reject confirmation if that version changed; await onDelete before showing deleted state and calling onDeleted. A deletion failure stays in ConfirmDialog.
Prevent overlapping save/delete operations with an operation ref; abort the current signal on unmount. Changing recordId remounts the session and intentionally discards its local draft.
Honor AbortSignal when possible and guard record identity changes with a navigation policy. Aborting client observation does not undo an already committed server mutation.

The host must enforce optimistic concurrency on the server or other authoritative persistence boundary.
Record identity changes intentionally reset the session; same-version record changes violate the host version contract.
Native fieldset disabling does not disable portaled controls; renderFields.disabled is provided for that boundary.

entries.summary: A router-neutral adapter for explicitly guarded navigation and a best-effort unload warning.

document.purpose: Adapt explicit host navigation requests to an unsaved-change confirmation with a bounded browser unload warning.
document.behaviorProvider: Native React composition with existing shared Aegis controls; see explicit component and host responsibilities.

confirmation and pending state
beforeunload listener lifecycle
host: dirty state and edited data
routing every guarded transition through the adapter
discard callback and navigation effects

requirements.statement: Expose requestNavigation(callback) from both the hook and render-prop component. A clean request runs without a dialog; a dirty request opens shared ConfirmDialog.
Call requestNavigation for every transition that should be guarded. The adapter does not intercept ordinary links, history APIs, browser back, or arbitrary SPA routers.
Accept one outstanding transition at a time. Concurrent requests resolve false rather than replacing the destination awaiting confirmation.
Cancel/dismiss resolves the pending request false without invoking its navigation callback. Unmount also settles an outstanding request false.
After confirmation, await onDiscard when still dirty, then invoke the stored navigation callback. Resolve true only after that callback completes.

For a confirmed guarded transition, thrown discard/navigation errors remain in ConfirmDialog and retain the same request for retry. A clean navigation rejection resolves false; the host owns its error presentation.
Attach beforeunload only while dirty and beforeUnload is enabled, and remove it when those conditions end or the component unmounts.
Treat beforeunload as a best-effort browser prompt: text, availability and user-activation requirements are browser-controlled. Persist or recover drafts independently when needed.
Make discard/navigation retry-safe and handle irreversible side effects; unmount stops subsequent work but cannot undo a navigation callback already running.
Use the shared ConfirmDialog for names, keyboard dismissal and focus return. Owned wrapper geometry uses workflow tokens.

limitations: No universal interception of router events, browser history or links.
Browser unload prompts may be suppressed and cannot show custom application text reliably.
An already running callback cannot be canceled or undone by unmount.
A retry may invoke onDiscard again; host callbacks must tolerate retries.

entries.name: TokenInput
entries.summary: Enter and remove multiple free-text values with atomic per-value validation and controlled host confirmation.

document.purpose: Enter and remove multiple free-text values with atomic per-value validation and controlled host confirmation.
invariants: A committed value is trimmed, Unicode NFC normalized and nonempty. Duplicate identity uses JavaScript lowercase after normalization.
Enter or Add commits; Shift+Enter inserts a newline. Blur commitment is off unless explicitly configured.
Newlines and tabs separate batch values. Commas remain literal unless comma is explicitly a commit key.
Every invalid batch is atomic: no values change and the exact submitted draft remains editable, including line breaks.
Duplicate reject is the default. Explicit ignore skips duplicates and announces their count.
Blank commit is a no-op. Validator accepts null/undefined; a nonempty string rejects; exceptions and other return types reject safely. Validators are synchronous.
In values confirmation mode a draft clears only when the host echoes the ordered requested values. This mode suits synchronous parents.

Asynchronous parents use request confirmation: accepted acknowledgment must match requestId AND requested ordered values; rejected acknowledgment preserves the draft. Stale acknowledgments never settle a newer request.
The host owns committed values and must honor the supplied AbortSignal when work is cancelled. This component cannot undo an authoritative stale host write.
Editing and restoring draft text still counts as a new draft. A delayed acceptance does not clear newer edits or steal focus.
Pending controls block additional mutations; draft remains editable. Keep editing aborts the pending request.
IME composition, native isComposing and keyCode229 prevent commit/removal. Holding Backspace does not remove values.
Empty-input Backspace arms removal; a second distinct press removes. Escape, blur or editing cancels the arm.
Suggestions are named buttons, preserve unrelated draft, and never restrict free-text entry. This is not a combobox.
Removal controls have accessible names; disabled state prevents user mutations.
document.behaviorProvider: native-textarea-plus-existing-components
document.asyncHostRequirement: Use confirmationMode=request and correlate acknowledgment IDs; discard results whose request signal is aborted.

component: atomic normalization/validation and keyboard draft lifecycle
request-correlated controlled confirmation
accessible input/token/suggestion feedback
host: authoritative ordered unique values
AbortSignal-aware async persistence and correlated acknowledgments
synchronous validation and error policy

requirements.statement: Trim candidate values, normalize Unicode NFC, discard empty candidates and compare duplicate identity with JavaScript lowercase after normalization. Incoming host values remain authoritative and are not silently normalized.

Default to duplicatePolicy=reject, commitKeys=[Enter], commitOnBlur=false and confirmationMode=values. Add or configured commit keys submit; Shift+Enter inserts a line, and only explicit comma commitment enables comma batch delimiting.

Split batches on newlines/tabs and optional commas. Apply synchronous per-value validation and duplicate policy atomically: any error leaves committed values unchanged and retains the exact submitted multiline draft.

Treat null/undefined as validation acceptance; require a nonempty string for rejection. Exceptions and other return types reject safely, and returned thenables are observed only to consume rejection rather than to accept an async result.

Blank text commits nothing. Reject duplicates by default; explicit ignore skips duplicates and announces the skipped count. An all-duplicate ignored batch clears its submitted draft without requesting a host change.

In values mode settle a pending change only when authoritative values match the complete ordered requested array. Clear submitted draft only if its captured revision still equals the current draft revision.

In request mode require a matching acknowledgment requestId before settling; rejection aborts and preserves the draft, while acceptance also requires the ordered requested values. Ignore stale acknowledgment IDs for newer pending requests.

While pending block further add/remove/suggestion mutations while keeping the draft editable. Keep editing aborts its signal and clears pending; unmount aborts any outstanding request. Disabled blocks user mutations and cancellation controls.
Count editing, including restoring identical text, as a new draft revision. Delayed confirmation cannot clear a newer draft and performs no programmatic focus transfer.

Ignore commit/removal during composition, native isComposing or keyCode229. Empty-input Backspace arms the last value; a second nonrepeat press requests removal. Escape, blur or normal draft editing cancels the arm; held Backspace does not repeatedly remove.

Render deduplicated suggestion strings as named ordinary buttons that preserve unrelated draft on commit, and values as a list of named removable Tags. This interface does not claim combobox/listbox navigation or restrict free-text entry.

Treat an immediate false return or thrown callback as refusal, abort the signal, preserve the draft and show safe feedback. Accepted mutations remain pending until the selected confirmation protocol is satisfied.

Use request mode for asynchronous writes, echo accepted ordered values plus a matching acknowledgment, and discard results whose signal is aborted. The callback returns void/false rather than a Promise; server concurrency and reversal of already-authoritative writes remain host responsibilities.

Provide ordered unique committed values and a meaningful label. The component has no named hidden form field or serialization API; persist/submit values through the host and keep external error content appropriate.

Use the retained evidence and migration references as historical bounded experiment records. Their status and source hashes do not rerun tests, certify this contract revision or establish human approval or stable release.
Use input group tokens for the owned entry layout and preserve nested Field, Textarea, Tag and Button categories, including visible focus in both modes.

limitations: Validation is synchronous and request completion is host-driven; no network request, server transaction or authoritative rollback is implemented.
Values confirmation cannot identify out-of-order async results; request mode and AbortSignal-aware hosts are required for that case.
Suggestions are optional action buttons rather than an ARIA combobox. No native form serialization is provided.

{
  "schemaVersion": 2,
  "id": "token-input",
  "version": 2,
  "status": "experimental",
  "verification": "bounded-automated-evidence-not-human-certification",
  "purpose": "Enter and remove multiple free-text values with atomic per-value validation and controlled host confirmation.",
  "anatomy": [
    "label",
    "input",
    "tokens",
    "error",
    "description",
    "add-control",
    "remove-controls",
    "suggestions",
    "status"
  ],
  "states": [
    "empty",
    "populated",
    "invalid",
    "disabled",
    "focus-visible",
    "pending-controlled-change",
    "composing"
  ],
  "invariants": [
    "A committed value is trimmed, Unicode NFC normalized and nonempty. Duplicate identity uses JavaScript lowercase after normalization.",
    "Enter or Add commits; Shift+Enter inserts a newline. Blur commitment is off unless explicitly configured.",
    "Newlines and tabs separate batch values. Commas remain literal unless comma is explicitly a commit key.",
    "Every invalid batch is atomic: no values change and the exact submitted draft remains editable, including line breaks.",
    "Duplicate reject is the default. Explicit ignore skips duplicates and announces their count.",
    "Blank commit is a no-op. Validator accepts null/undefined; a nonempty string rejects; exceptions and other return types reject safely. Validators are synchronous.",
    "In values confirmation mode a draft clears only when the host echoes the ordered requested values. This mode suits synchronous parents.",
    "Asynchronous parents use request confirmation: accepted acknowledgment must match requestId AND requested ordered values; rejected acknowledgment preserves the draft. Stale acknowledgments never settle a newer request.",
    "The host owns committed values and must honor the supplied AbortSignal when work is cancelled. This component cannot undo an authoritative stale host write.",
    "Editing and restoring draft text still counts as a new draft. A delayed acceptance does not clear newer edits or steal focus.",
    "Pending controls block additional mutations; draft remains editable. Keep editing aborts the pending request.",
    "IME composition, native isComposing and keyCode229 prevent commit/removal. Holding Backspace does not remove values.",
    "Empty-input Backspace arms removal; a second distinct press removes. Escape, blur or editing cancels the arm.",
    "Suggestions are named buttons, preserve unrelated draft, and never restrict free-text entry. This is not a combobox.",
    "Removal controls have accessible names; disabled state prevents user mutations."
  ],
  "tokenGroup": "input",
  "behaviorProvider": "native-textarea-plus-existing-components",
  "defaults": {
    "duplicatePolicy": "reject",
    "commitKeys": ["Enter"],
    "commitOnBlur": false,
    "confirmationMode": "values"
  },
  "asyncHostRequirement": "Use confirmationMode=request and correlate acknowledgment IDs; discard results whose request signal is aborted.",
  "evidence": "experiments/token-input/consolidated/evidence.json",
  "migration": "experiments/token-input/consolidated/MIGRATION.md",
  "ownership": {
    "component": [
      "atomic normalization/validation and keyboard draft lifecycle",
      "request-correlated controlled confirmation",
      "accessible input/token/suggestion feedback"
    ],
    "host": [
      "authoritative ordered unique values",
      "AbortSignal-aware async persistence and correlated acknowledgments",
      "synchronous validation and error policy"
    ]
  },
  "requirements": [
    {
      "id": "normalization-and-identity",
      "kind": "component",
      "statement": "Trim candidate values, normalize Unicode NFC, discard empty candidates and compare duplicate identity with JavaScript lowercase after normalization. Incoming host values remain authoritative and are not silently normalized.",
      "sources": [
        "src/agentic/components/TokenInput.tsx",
        "src/agentic/components/token-input-model.ts"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "commit-defaults",
      "kind": "component",
      "statement": "Default to duplicatePolicy=reject, commitKeys=[Enter], commitOnBlur=false and confirmationMode=values. Add or configured commit keys submit; Shift+Enter inserts a line, and only explicit comma commitment enables comma batch delimiting.",
      "sources": ["src/agentic/components/TokenInput.tsx"]
    },
    {
      "id": "atomic-batch",
      "kind": "component",
      "statement": "Split batches on newlines/tabs and optional commas. Apply synchronous per-value validation and duplicate policy atomically: any error leaves committed values unchanged and retains the exact submitted multiline draft.",
      "sources": [
        "src/agentic/components/TokenInput.tsx",
        "src/agentic/components/token-input-model.ts"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "validator-contract",
      "kind": "component",
      "statement": "Treat null/undefined as validation acceptance; require a nonempty string for rejection. Exceptions and other return types reject safely, and returned thenables are observed only to consume rejection rather than to accept an async result.",
      "sources": [
        "src/agentic/components/TokenInput.tsx",
        "src/agentic/components/token-input-model.ts"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "duplicate-and-blank-policy",
      "kind": "component",
      "statement": "Blank text commits nothing. Reject duplicates by default; explicit ignore skips duplicates and announces the skipped count. An all-duplicate ignored batch clears its submitted draft without requesting a host change.",
      "sources": [
        "src/agentic/components/TokenInput.tsx",
        "src/agentic/components/token-input-model.ts"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "values-confirmation",
      "kind": "component",
      "statement": "In values mode settle a pending change only when authoritative values match the complete ordered requested array. Clear submitted draft only if its captured revision still equals the current draft revision.",
      "sources": ["src/agentic/components/TokenInput.tsx"]
    },
    {
      "id": "request-confirmation",
      "kind": "component",
      "statement": "In request mode require a matching acknowledgment requestId before settling; rejection aborts and preserves the draft, while acceptance also requires the ordered requested values. Ignore stale acknowledgment IDs for newer pending requests.",
      "sources": ["src/agentic/components/TokenInput.tsx"]
    },
    {
      "id": "pending-and-cancel",
      "kind": "component",
      "statement": "While pending block further add/remove/suggestion mutations while keeping the draft editable. Keep editing aborts its signal and clears pending; unmount aborts any outstanding request. Disabled blocks user mutations and cancellation controls.",
      "sources": ["src/agentic/components/TokenInput.tsx"]
    },
    {
      "id": "draft-revision",
      "kind": "component",
      "statement": "Count editing, including restoring identical text, as a new draft revision. Delayed confirmation cannot clear a newer draft and performs no programmatic focus transfer.",
      "sources": ["src/agentic/components/TokenInput.tsx"]
    },
    {
      "id": "keyboard-removal",
      "kind": "component",
      "statement": "Ignore commit/removal during composition, native isComposing or keyCode229. Empty-input Backspace arms the last value; a second nonrepeat press requests removal. Escape, blur or normal draft editing cancels the arm; held Backspace does not repeatedly remove.",
      "sources": ["src/agentic/components/TokenInput.tsx"]
    },
    {
      "id": "suggestions-and-removal",
      "kind": "component",
      "statement": "Render deduplicated suggestion strings as named ordinary buttons that preserve unrelated draft on commit, and values as a list of named removable Tags. This interface does not claim combobox/listbox navigation or restrict free-text entry.",
      "sources": ["src/agentic/components/TokenInput.tsx"]
    },
    {
      "id": "immediate-refusal",
      "kind": "component",
      "statement": "Treat an immediate false return or thrown callback as refusal, abort the signal, preserve the draft and show safe feedback. Accepted mutations remain pending until the selected confirmation protocol is satisfied.",
      "sources": ["src/agentic/components/TokenInput.tsx"]
    },
    {
      "id": "host-async-policy",
      "kind": "host",
      "statement": "Use request mode for asynchronous writes, echo accepted ordered values plus a matching acknowledgment, and discard results whose signal is aborted. The callback returns void/false rather than a Promise; server concurrency and reversal of already-authoritative writes remain host responsibilities.",
      "sources": ["src/agentic/components/TokenInput.tsx"]
    },
    {
      "id": "host-value-and-form",
      "kind": "host",
      "statement": "Provide ordered unique committed values and a meaningful label. The component has no named hidden form field or serialization API; persist/submit values through the host and keep external error content appropriate.",
      "sources": ["src/agentic/components/TokenInput.tsx"]
    },
    {
      "id": "historical-evidence",
      "kind": "host",
      "statement": "Use the retained evidence and migration references as historical bounded experiment records. Their status and source hashes do not rerun tests, certify this contract revision or establish human approval or stable release.",
      "sources": [
        "src/agentic/components/TokenInput.tsx",
        "experiments/token-input/consolidated/evidence.json",
        "experiments/token-input/consolidated/MIGRATION.md"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "nested-token-ownership",
      "kind": "design",
      "statement": "Use input group tokens for the owned entry layout and preserve nested Field, Textarea, Tag and Button categories, including visible focus in both modes.",
      "sources": ["src/agentic/components/TokenInput.tsx", "skills/references/design-contract.md"]
    }
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Validation is synchronous and request completion is host-driven; no network request, server transaction or authoritative rollback is implemented.",
    "Values confirmation cannot identify out-of-order async results; request mode and AbortSignal-aware hosts are required for that case.",
    "Suggestions are optional action buttons rather than an ARIA combobox. No native form serialization is provided.",
    "Historical evidence remains unchanged and can report a source-hash mismatch after this documentation/schema upgrade; mismatch is not silently relabelled as a current pass."
  ]
}

contract.raw:
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "name": "Aegis authenticated shared workspace protocol",
  "basePath": "/api/aegis-workspace",
  "deployment": "single-host-local-filesystem",
  "defaultPort": 4178,
  "authentication": {
    "scheme": "Bearer",
    "transport": "Authorization header only",
    "storage": "SHA-256 token hash",
    "roles": ["admin", "owner", "operator", "viewer", "ingest"],
    "expiryRequired": true
  },
  "requestRules": {
    "maximumBodyBytes": 65536,
    "maximumRequestsPerMinutePerConnectionAddress": 240,
    "unknownFields": "reject",
    "queries": "reject",
    "mutations": { "Content-Type": "application/json", "X-Aegis-Client": ["console", "sdk"] }
  },
  "endpoints": [
    {
      "method": "GET",
      "path": "/healthz",
      "relativeTo": "service-root",
      "authentication": false,
      "response": "minimal readiness only"
    },
    {
      "method": "GET",
      "path": "/projects",
      "role": "read-capable",
      "response": "scoped projects and actor label/role"
    },
    {
      "method": "POST",
      "path": "/projects",
      "role": "admin",
      "body": ["id", "name", "kitDigest", "profile"]
    },
    { "method": "GET", "path": "/kits", "role": "admin" },
    { "method": "GET", "path": "/audit", "role": "admin" },
    { "method": "GET", "path": "/maintenance", "role": "admin" },
    { "method": "POST", "path": "/maintenance", "role": "admin", "body": { "action": "resume" } },
    { "method": "GET", "path": "/projects/:id/status", "role": "scoped-reader" },
    { "method": "GET", "path": "/projects/:id/configurability", "role": "scoped-reader" },
    { "method": "GET", "path": "/projects/:id/generations", "role": "scoped-reader" },
    { "method": "GET", "path": "/projects/:id/audit", "role": "scoped-reader" },
    {
      "method": "POST",
      "path": "/projects/:id/plan",
      "role": "scoped-operator",
      "optionalBody": ["useAI"]
    },
    { "method": "POST", "path": "/projects/:id/reconcile", "role": "scoped-operator", "body": [] },
    { "method": "POST", "path": "/projects/:id/retention", "role": "scoped-operator", "body": [] },
    {
      "method": "POST",
      "path": "/projects/:id/telemetry",
      "role": "scoped-operator",
      "body": ["enabled"]
    },
    {
      "method": "POST",
      "path": "/projects/:id/usage",
      "role": "admin-or-scoped-ingest",
      "body": ["events", "batchId"]
    },
    {
      "method": "POST",
      "path": "/projects/:id/updates",
      "role": "scoped-owner",
      "body": ["expectedRevision", "kitDigest", "profile"]
    },
    {
      "method": "POST",
      "path": "/projects/:id/rollback",
      "role": "scoped-owner",
      "body": ["generationId", "expectedRevision"]
    },
    {
      "method": "POST",
      "path": "/projects/:id/activate",
      "role": "scoped-owner",
      "body": ["planId", "planDigest", "expectedRevision", "reason"]
    }
  ],
  "invariants": [
    "kits verified before runtime import",
    "signed releases required by default",
    "prepared plans expire after 24 hours",
    "activation uses compare-and-swap revision and new generation",
    "activation disables collection and AI",
    "rollback is prepared then reviewed",
    "service never auto-activates updates",
    "no remote model calls from maintenance loops"
  ],
  "errors": {
    "400": "invalid request",
    "401": "missing, expired or revoked credential",
    "403": "role/scope/origin/host/client marker refused",
    "409": "integrity, revision, lock or validation conflict",
    "413": "body too large",
    "415": "not JSON",
    "429": "request budget exceeded"
  }
}
